_readme: TopCoat HQ Dashboard feature manifest. One entry per shipped feature: plain-English description (catalog quality) plus code anchors. Consult before grepping index.html. Anchors are FUNCTION NAMES, never line numbers. Update the relevant entry when shipping changes to a feature (CLAUDE.md rule 9). Generated 2026-07-18.

features.name: In-house estimator PWA
features.description: A mobile, installable estimating app that reps use in the driveway to price coating jobs from square footage and system type using the same catalog and margin math as job costing. It works fully offline (service worker plus local cache with a sync outbox) so an estimate built with no signal saves and uploads once the phone reconnects. Prompt 47: a new estimate defaults its salesperson to the LOGGED-IN rep, mapped explicitly by pec_sales_team_members.auth_user_id (set per member in Settings > Sales Team via openSalesTeamModal's Login picker; migration 2026-07-22_sales_member_auth_user.sql). An unmapped login gets a blank salesperson plus a get-mapped prompt, never a silent first-in-list fallback. Prompt 55 NARROWS prompt 47: once a salesperson is set, the select is read-only text for non-admins (admin check = admin_users.role threaded from App.tsx, FAIL CLOSED); the blank/unmapped case stays editable for everyone so the get-mapped path never dead-ends. Shared rules (draft gate, trigger, default priority) live in production/estimate-draft.cjs, fixture-tested. Prompt 61 (Part A): the estimator's NORMAL home is now INLINE on the estimate detail page (no modal); the app posts its content height (pec-estimator-height, ResizeObserver + rAF) so the page grows instead of nesting scrollbars, follows the DASHBOARD's theme via pec-theme postMessage (never the OS), drops its duplicated header chrome when embedded, and its styles.css mirrors the dashboard's --rd-* design tokens (PEC orange, same surfaces/ink/lines) so the panel reads as part of the page. A draft loaded with zero areas seeds the create-path Main area (initialAreas in estimate-draft.cjs, fixture-tested). The old #pecModalRoot modal remains ONLY as the offline create fallback; the standalone /estimator/ page and the offline outbox are untouched. Prompt 62 (Part H): the More detail accordion is gone; products, colors, and the work order questions render always visible in both standard and custom modes. special_notes is retired in favor of the one 8-row 'Notes for the crew' box bound to estimates.crew_notes (saves no longer write intake.special_notes; old rows keep the key). A blank moisture or MOHS raises an unmissable red banner (wo-banner) on the estimator and the estimate detail page; save and send are never blocked. Prompt 63 (Parts A + C) NARROWS prompt 62 Part H: the work order questions stay always visible, but every product-kind slot (kindOf === 'product': Basecoat, Topcoat, Flake, Quartz, and any future product material_type) is HIDDEN at estimate time behind a small 'Specify products' link (session-only reveal for all areas, collapsed again on every open); choice/text slots like Topcoat cure speed and the system picker stay. Display-only: slotValues keeps the prefilled defaults, so pricing and the saved estimate_area_materials rows are identical either way, but estimates.flake_color is now normally NULL at estimate time (swatch slots are unprefilled by design; the estimate page's manual Flake color field is the writer). Part C: body.embed #root { height: auto } lets the embedded frame SHRINK as well as grow (the height reporter measures #root.scrollHeight, which at height:100% could never report less than the frame, so short estimates showed a ratcheted blank gap). Prompt 76: the per-area stacked cards and separate Add-ons card collapsed into ONE compact Line items table; tapping a row opens a bottom-sheet line editor (BottomSheet.tsx, the estimator's OWN modal lifecycle with escape/focus-trap/scroll-lock; full-height sheet under estimator_line_sheet_breakpoint_px, centered window above it; embed-aware positioning computes the iframe's visible slice from window.frameElement and locks the parent page's scroll). The whole-document Proposal/Scope textarea is gone; per-line descriptions are the editable scope now. Prompt 82: the Save button ALWAYS renders, in both modes and at every viewport, outside every pricing gate; when the estimate cannot be saved the button is disabled with the first blocker named beside it in plain English (saveBlockers in EstimatorScreen.tsx, the single source of truth canSave derives from: salesperson, customer identity, per-line prices, sqft/system on calculator lines, engine errors, MVB product, override reason, add-on completeness). performSave's guards also stopped returning null silently; a tripped guard sets the save error state with the blocker text. Auto-seeded payment schedule (2026-08-18): new estimates pre-fill the default schedule once a price exists, re-seeding on dominant-system change until the rep touches a row. Prompt 84 (2026-08-10): the estimator STOPPED writing estimates.status on edits. status rides saveEstimateOffline's row ONLY on the save that creates the row (the early draft card or a first Save; SaveEstimateArgs.status is optional now); an edit's upsert leaves the column alone, so a save queued offline before a send can no longer replay a stale 'draft' over a row the dashboard flipped to 'sent' (the EST-102054 clobber). The dashboard's markEstimateSent owns the sent flip, and the trg_estimate_status_guard trigger (2026-08-19 migration) refuses status regressions at the database as the backstop for old cached clients. DripJobs-shape editor (2026-08-10 phase 4): Estimate type and Salesperson share one card, Comps and the AI price read are collapsed disclosures under the Money card (the Save row stays always-rendered in the rail, the prompt-82 invariant), and a full-width Settings | Notes tab strip sits below the columns: Settings holds the payment schedule editor plus a read-only deposit-percent summary naming its source; Notes holds three lanes with visibility badges: Crew notes [TEAM ONLY] (estimates.crew_notes, AI generate intact), Client notes [CLIENT VISIBLE] (estimates.client_notes, renders on the customer page), Company notes [INTERNAL ONLY] (estimates.company_notes).

features.name: Numbered estimate records
features.description: Every saved estimate becomes a sequential, searchable record (EST-102026 and up) with its own page showing customer info, price and margin, line items, optional add-ons, flake color, and the comps and AI price read behind the number. A dedicated Estimates list holds them all, and estimates can be archived and restored as a soft delete. Prompt 38: estimates can now be TEXTED as well as emailed. The same split Send control as invoices (default both channels); the text goes through pec-send-sms kind='estimate' (server-built body with the /e/<token> review-and-sign link + STOP line, lead/customer opt-out enforced, logged to pec_sms_log kind 'estimate' so it stays out of Last-invoiced), and a text-only send runs the same markEstimateSent flip + estimateSentLeadEffects as email so the estimate goes live either way. The blank-scope warn gate fires on any channel. Prompt 47 (card first): the estimate ROW now exists the moment the rep makes their first real edit in the estimator, written by an early draft save (parent row only, requires name/phone/email/address/salesperson, all prefilled in the lead flow) under the same pre-minted id the full Save upserts. Draft-status estimates show an 'In Draft' badge on the list rows and the detail header (the shared EST_STATUS_META draft label; numbering stays the Postgres sequence, so an unnumbered card reads '(unnumbered)' until its first sync). Prompt 61 (Parts A-C): New estimate / Start estimate now INSERTS the draft row immediately (duplicate guard via leadOpenEstimates BEFORE the insert; job info prefilled onto the row from the lead in both split and legacy column shapes) and lands on the estimate detail page with the estimator open inline; a sent/signed/rejected estimate renders the read-only summary with Edit swapping the estimator in on the page. renderEstimateDetail guards landmine 1 at its top: while the inline estimator is alive, refreshes rebuild the chrome and summary around the untouched iframe, so no handler can reload the PWA and drop typed work. The job info block (#estJobInfo) is natively editable (renderEstJobInfoBlock): split + composed legacy columns written in the estimator's exact shape, salesperson admin-locked fail-closed with intake read-modify-written whole, and propagation to the linked lead/customer is ASK EACH TIME with pre-checked boxes (lead_events 'lead_updated' records it; a declined push shows a differs-from-lead note with one-click Push to lead). The authority rule is stated on the page: the estimate carries its own snapshot; lead and customer change only on a yes. Abandoned empty drafts are left alone (Dylan archives by hand) and estimate-number gaps are accepted; leadValueMapFrom skips priceless rows so an early draft never zeroes a lead's value. Prompt 62 (Part E): starting an estimate from the Estimates list opens a three-path picker: existing customer (estimates.customer_id set, lead_id null), existing lead (unchanged, duplicate guard before the insert, the lead's customer_id carried along), or a new customer created inline with the Individual/Business name rules. Draft prefill also works from a customer row; the detail page links the customer when there is no lead; on accept, pec-public-estimate resolves the customer by estimates.customer_id first so a no-lead estimate converts to a job directly. A blank moisture or MOHS reading raises a red banner on the detail page (and in the estimator); never a block. Prompt 65 (Part B): the three-path picker became ONE contact-first New Estimate modal in the DripJobs New Proposal shape, used at every entry point (openEstimateStartPicker, called by the Estimates list button and by Start estimate on an appointment): a Contact dropdown defaulting to New Contact with existing customers and leads (Leads optgroup, stage-labeled) below it, a read-only summary when an existing record is picked (the modal never edits that record), the prompt 62 name + required-lead-source rules for New Contact, a display-only 'In Draft' stage (estimates has NO stage column, deliberately), an editable Job Address block (prefilled from the picked record's address, written to BOTH the split customer_address1/city/state/zip columns AND the legacy combined customer_address), and a Salesperson select defaulting to the login's mapped pec_sales_team_members row (auth_user_id, prompt 47) whose pick lands in intake.salesperson_id/_name composed inside the brand-new insert only (never a partial-intake PATCH). createDraftEstimate/createDraftEstimateNow accept an extras override ({address, salesperson, crewNotes}) applied on top of the record prefill; the lead path keeps the duplicate guard BEFORE the insert. Part C: Start estimate in the appointment edit modal footer routes lead -> guarded create, customer-only -> direct create, unlinked -> this modal on New Contact prefilled from the appointment; the appointment's location_* address wins over the customer's billing address and its customer_notes land in estimates.crew_notes. Prompt 65 follow-up (Dylan-approved 2026-08-03): the salesperson lock loosened on BOTH surfaces (renderEstJobInfoBlock and the estimator) with the same rule: the estimate's CREATOR (created_by matches the login) may change the salesperson while status='draft' and sent_at is null; the lock lands at send. Fail-closed unchanged: errored role read, null created_by, or missing session keeps the lock for non-admins. Cross-nav (2026-08-10): when the estimate has a job (estimates.job_id, set by ensureJobCreated on accept), the detail toolbar shows Open job and View invoice buttons, gated on job_id ONLY (not signed_at, which is what hid the old buried banner link); both confirm before navigating if the inline estimator is open on this estimate.

features.name: Customer-facing estimate (send, sign, accept)
features.description: Reps send a private link where the customer reviews the scope and line items, ticks optional add-ons with a live-updating total, and accepts by typing their name to sign, or requests changes or declines with a reason. Accepting automatically creates the job on both the Jobs page and the Job Schedule with all areas and work-order details carried over, including a custom estimate's typed square footage (into the job's sqft) and the internal crew notes. A Preview button shows the exact customer page before sending; the preview modal (prompt 63 Part D) has a header bar with the estimate number and a ✕, and closes on ✕, Escape, or backdrop click via openModal's opt-in dismissible flag (data-entry modals keep their stray-click/Escape protection; the offline estimator fallback modal has a confirm-gated ✕ only). Prompt 69: on accept every job_areas row now carries its line's final price and scope description, and a custom line becomes a real job_areas row (name from custom_label, no system) so the crew sees it on the work order. Prompt 72: the page renders 'Your project' (required lines, no checkbox, plus pre-selected optional lines with a ticked toggle) and 'Options to add'; accept guards against a zero-selection POST; on a partial accept the job is built from the selected areas only and declined lines stay on the estimate as the record. See 'Optional line items on any line'. Prompt 74: the page renders DripJobs-proposal style. Every line shows its label, a sq ft subtitle derived from its area (plus the MVB note), and its FULL scope of work expanded under the line inside a zero-JS details/summary collapse (print always expands); the whole-document scope render is gone (estimates.scope_of_work is internal-only now). The reading order is header, prepared-for, scope summary table, Your project, Options to add, Your investment (subtotal + project total + emphasized balance line), payment schedule, financing, terms and conditions (per-brand pec_brand_identity.estimate_terms_text in a scrollable box above the signature; no card when empty), then signature/actions and literature. A hard send gate on every channel (email, text, Present's Open for signing) blocks while scope_stale is true, any scope-bearing line has an empty description or the old sqft clobber fingerprint, or the payment schedule does not resolve to the estimate total; the block names the offending lines. After signing, the accepted banner offers 'Pay your deposit now' linking the existing pay page (resolveCurrentAsk amount, card + ACH, no surcharge, never auto-redirect; absent when no deposit row exists). Prompt 77 (2026-08-08): pec_brand_identity now has a 'finishing-touch' row (FTP name, shared PEC address/phone, FTP accent #ff6b1a; license_number and estimate_terms_text deliberately NULL, so no ROC number and no terms card render on FTP paperwork until Dylan fills them in Settings > Brand), and loadBrand/notifyOffice normalize est.brand's short forms ('PEC'/'FTP') through presentationBrandKey before the pec_brand_identity / pec_email_senders lookups, so an FTP estimate picks up FTP's identity instead of silently falling through to PEC's. Prompt 78: the Preview modal is TICKABLE. The one interactive flag split into two: ticking (checkboxes + live recalc, true on any OPEN estimate including a staff preview) and interactive (the public token + accept/change/decline actions, live page only), emitted as two sections of one IIFE so a preview render can never leak the public token (previewing an accepted estimate stays fully read-only). The top summary table (system / combined sqft / MVB / flake color) is gone; flake color survives as a one-line note above 'Your project' (a combined footage lies when the lines carry different systems; footage stays per line). Customer ticks persist immediately via the debounced fire-and-forget 'select' action (same applySelection writer as accept), and estimates.price + GP settle ONCE when the customer first opens the accept panel (signing:true), status-guarded so a mid-flight signature can never be clobbered; GP is skipped entirely (stored values untouched, warn logged) if any included priced line has no unit_cost, and gp_pct is stored as a fraction matching the estimator convention. Residue Dylan accepted: an abandoned accept panel leaves price mid-range on an open estimate (degrades gracefully; the up-to render keys on price != price_all_options). Prompt 81: the send composer no longer carries the CTA button inside the Quill editor (Quill 2 strips anchor styling, which is why customers were receiving a bare blue link); the fixed View & sign your estimate button is appended by the send path after the editor content, styled by emailCtaButtonHtml from pec_brand_identity.accent_color, and a note under the editor says so. 2026-08-10: the accepted banner now asks HOW the customer wants to pay whatever is currently due (card/bank via Stripe Checkout with the amount resolved server-side at click time, check/cash/Zelle intent buttons riding /api/invoice/intent, and a Financing jump link to the Ways-to-pay card). The old deposit-only gate (payCta null unless the deposit installment was the current ask) is gone: the chooser shows for ANY positive current ask, falling back to the pay page's legacy deposit/balance rule when no schedule rows exist. Kill switch: settings post_sign_payment_prompt_enabled (missing = on), toggled on Settings > Invoicing. Prompt 84 (2026-08-10): the derived sent-state rule the pipeline always used (a status='draft' row WITH a sent_at HAS been sent) is now the shared helper estimateEffectiveStatus(est), routed through every surface that keys on draft-vs-sent: the pipeline's estColOf, the estimates list, the detail page's status badge and send-button gating, the lead card's estimate rows, global search, the duplicate-estimate modal, the kanban Draft chip set, the salesperson unlock rule, and the detail page's draft auto-open. No surface keys on the raw status column alone. The detail page also shows an 'edited after send' notice when a sendable estimate's client_updated_at is newer than its sent_at (the customer's link already shows the new numbers); its Re-send button clicks the existing toolbar send kit, never a second send path. Prompt 84 commit 2 (2026-08-10): an EMPTY estimate is a hard send block on every channel, no override. Empty means zero line items OR an opening total that is null or zero (either one blocks; EST-102075, a pre-minted hollow draft card, was emailed and texted to a real customer because every existing blocker came out of the line-item loop and zero items produced zero blockers). The client rule is the FIRST blocker in estimateSendGateOk (email, text, and Present's Open for signing all route through it); the server mirror is emptySendError in production/optional-lines.cjs, enforced by pec-send-sms.cjs on the estimate-token lookup and by pec-send-email.cjs via the new optional compose-mode estimate_id the dashboard passes on estimate sends (a compose send with no estimate_id behaves exactly as before). Investment block (2026-08-10, DripJobs-parity phase 5): the Your investment summary shows Subtotal, an accent-tinted Deposit to start row, and a full-width brand-accent band with Project total left and the closing balance (last schedule row) right; the deposit row and band values live-update as the customer ticks optional lines (the deposit cell is a passive mirror keyed by the deposit's schedule index, never an extra data-sched cell, so the joint remainder allocation stays exact). Accepted pages render the frozen signature schedule values. Client note (2026-08-20): a non-empty estimates.client_notes renders as an 'A note from us' block above the line items; crew and company notes never render.

features.name: Estimate view tracking
features.description: Every customer open of the public estimate page is logged (link-preview bots from SMS/email apps filtered by user agent). On every logged open a Slack alert posts to #epoxysales with the customer, estimate number, price, salesperson, which open it is, and time since sent (its own switch, estimate_view_slack_enabled, default on; never throttled). When bell notifications are enabled, each open also drops a shared bell row for all staff plus a personal bell row for the salesperson on the estimate (resolved through the intake salesperson chain; pec_notifications.target_user_id, a display filter, not privacy); both bell rows share the optional first-view-per-day throttle. The estimate card's Customer view section shows a full view block: count, first and last open with relative times, the latest 10 individual opens, and a Hot chip when the shared hot rule is met (views >= estimate_hot_min_views with the last inside estimate_hot_window_hours; defaults 3/48, tunable in Settings > Estimates). A sent estimate with zero opens says Not opened yet. Prompt 78: bell rows lead with the customer's name plus the view ordinal ('Susan Nasser viewed estimate #102064 (2nd view)'), resolved through customerDisplay so a commercial estimate shows the company name; the rep bell drops the redundant 'Your customer' prefix. Write-time string change only; existing rows keep their wording, no backfill.

features.name: Estimator duplicate-customer search
features.description: A search box on the estimator's customer card finds existing customers and leads by name, phone, email, or address as the rep types, labeling each result Customer or Lead with phone and address. Picking a match prefills the form and links the estimate through estimates.lead_id (a customer match reuses or creates its lead via leads.customer_id), so no duplicate record is created. Online-only; offline the search hides and the outbox save path is unchanged. Toggle in Settings > Estimates (estimator_customer_search_enabled).

features.name: Auto-written scope of work
features.description: Estimates assemble a polished, customer-facing scope of work from the company's real templates, filling in square footage, areas, and inclusions from the estimate itself while never altering exclusions or cure-time language. The estimator prompts reps to fill any template blanks on site, warns before a blank reaches the customer, and the AI writes the final version once, then only rewrites on an explicit Regenerate so hand edits are preserved. Prompt 69: each area's internal notes ride that line's generation context as substitution facts (never quoted into customer text, never new scope), and a custom line's typed scope is used VERBATIM (the writer skips it; only the explicit Polish button touches custom text). Prompt 74: the per-line descriptions the writer assembles are now the CUSTOMER-FACING scope under each line, and the estimator's save never authors them (the old save wrote '970 sqft' over every calculator line's description on each re-save, erasing generated scope on sent estimates; descriptions now round-trip through lineDescription and a new line starts null until generation fills it). The send gate hard-blocks an estimate whose scope is stale or missing per line. Prompt 76: every line's description is EDITABLE in the line editor sheet (templates seed it, a rep edit WINS until the rep presses Generate again; the post-generation refresh skips lines edited this session). The writer's templateless skip branch now CLEARS a description matching the exact sqft clobber fingerprint (CLOBBER_DESC_EXACT_RE) and returns per-line skip reasons (area_id + needs_rep_text) that the sheet shows, so a templateless system is a type-it-here prompt instead of a dead end. The whole-document scope UI was deleted from both the estimator and the estimate detail (estimates.scope_of_work is still written and still feeds jobScope, the crew scope, and the declined filter); Regenerate scope lives on the Line items card, and send-gate blockers are tappable links that open the offending line's sheet with the description focused (the gate re-reads rows fresh). Settings: estimate_line_generate_enabled, estimator_line_sheet_breakpoint_px. 2026-08-08: Dylan approved scope templates for Metallic (4 day system, hardcoded not-included lines at his choice) and MVB Only; both were seeded live. The MVB-only scope exemption (writer skip + send-gate pass + estimator no-scope-needed chip) is retired: MVB Only lines generate and gate like any other area line.

features.name: Multi-system estimates
features.description: One estimate can cover several areas that each carry their own system (a flake garage plus a quartz patio), priced with each area's own recipe and rolled into a single price. The gross-profit target is the square-foot-weighted average of the systems in play so a small high-margin area does not skew the whole number. Prompt 69 REPLACES the estimator's sqft-weighted single-divisor solve: each area now solves its own price at its own system's rates and the job total is the sum (see 'Per-line pricing and custom lines'); a single-area estimate prices identically to the cent, and the dashboard's change-order pricer still uses computeEstimatePricing (single-area, unaffected).

features.name: Add-ons catalog
features.description: Reps drop upsells like stem walls, joint filling, upgrades, or drive time onto an estimate from a managed catalog, each with a prefilled price, real cost, unit, and scope paragraph. Because every add-on carries a cost, gross profit stays honest, and items marked optional stay out of the base total until the customer selects them.

features.name: Estimate pricing engine and controls
features.description: Estimates price from just the system and square footage using recipe default products and a per-system target gross profit, then show the full work behind the number: price per square foot, the cost stack (materials, labor, sundries, add-ons, commission, gross profit), and a plain-English explanation including charm rounding. Reps can override the sell price with a required reason and a floor confirmation, every estimate bakes in an adjustable 2% sundries cost, and moisture vapor barrier is chosen per area. Prompt 66: comps GP% comes from the ONE canonical formula (production/costing.js computeCostingRow, mirrored byte-identical in index.html), fed by real cost tables (pec_prod_material_lines used materials, pec_prod_job_bonuses, BusyBusy/manual hours with loaded labor incl. burden via buildCostAggregates); a comp with no cost signal shows a dash and the caveat reads 'GP% shown for N of M comps'. Prompt 69: the override-reason rule is threshold-gated (required only when the final total lands under the calculated total by more than the greater of line_pricing_reason_threshold_pct/_dollars, whether via per-line edits or the job discount), and a per-line GP floor (line_pricing_gp_floor_pct) reddens individual lines. Prompt 70: the comps panel never shows cross-system jobs anymore (hard filter) and the AI read is per line; see 'Per-line AI price read and hard-filtered comps'.

features.name: Custom estimate mode
features.description: A Standard/Custom switch lets reps price one-off work that does not fit the material calculator by typing the scope and price themselves, with add-ons still available. An optional Polish with AI button cleans up the typed scope wording without changing meaning, exclusions, or dollar figures, and can be undone. An optional square footage field shows a live read-only price per sqft (the price stays the typed number) and carries to the job's sqft on accept, lighting up the $/sqft readouts on Job Costing and the work order. Prompt 58: the Work order site questions (gate code, moisture, MOHS, tooling, non-slip, coat past garage, stem walls, special notes) render in custom mode too, from one shared field list. A blank Moisture or MOHS shows a soft warning on the estimator (near the grid and by both save rows) and on the job page's Job Card; it never blocks save, send, or accept. Prompt 69 adds custom LINES inside a normal estimate (mixed quartz-plus-one-off proposals) without touching this whole-estimate mode; see 'Per-line pricing and custom lines'. Prompt 76: the separate Polish button is renamed and folded into the one Generate with AI button (same polish endpoint, same undo), matching the per-line editor.

features.name: Per-line pricing and custom lines
features.description: Prompt 69: every estimate line prices on its own. Each calculator area solves its OWN cost-plus price at its own system's labor% and target GP% (computePerLinePricing in production/calculator.js: ONE estimate-wide kit-merged material plan, attributed back to areas by pre-merge raw cost via allocateProportionally, so shared kits are never double-bought), and the job total is the sum of the lines; the old back-allocation of a single job price is gone. A CUSTOM LINE is an estimate_areas row (is_custom=true) with a typed label, verbatim scope, typed price (stored in price_override), typed material cost and crew hours, so its GP is computed like every other line; it pulls no catalog products and adds nothing to the material plan. Per-line GP shows on each line and goes red under the line_pricing_gp_floor_pct floor (line_pricing_block_below_floor decides warn vs forced confirm, and the save confirmation NAMES the below-floor lines). The job-level sell/discount allocates across the lines proportionally (parts sum to the typed total exactly), and a written reason is required whenever the final total lands under the CALCULATED total by more than the greater of line_pricing_reason_threshold_pct / line_pricing_reason_threshold_dollars, no matter how the rep got there. Per-line internal notes feed that line's scope generation and never render customer-facing. On accept, each job_areas row carries its line's final price and scope description; a custom line becomes a real job_areas row (custom_label, no system) but is skipped in pec_prod_areas (recipe side, NOT NULL sqft/system). Settings live in Settings > Estimates > Line pricing. Whole-estimate Custom mode (build 24) is unchanged. Prompt 70 built the per-line AI on top of this: each line's recommendation keys off the seams this build left (pricing_snapshot.ai.lines[].line_key, cheaply hashable per-line inputs). Prompt 72 builds on this: any of these lines can now be marked optional for the customer, and the per-line GP feeds the required-only GP warning. Prompt 76: the line list renders as a compact table and each line's full controls (name, system, sqft, MVB, price, optional flags, description, internal notes) live in the tap-to-open bottom-sheet editor. Prompt 82: a custom-line-only estimate is a FIRST-CLASS priceable estimate. The engine is required only when a calculator line exists (lineRowsReady in production/calculator.js); with only custom lines the engine stays dormant, the typed prices sum to the job total, GP/labor/commission/sundries compute from each line's typed cost basis, and the save writes null engine columns and a null system (dominantSystemId '' is coerced to null so the uuid column never sees an empty string). The pct labels in the money panel fall back to config values when the engine is dormant (labor shows the $/hr rate), the derivation line reads 'N custom lines at typed prices', and the misleading 'give at least one area a system and square footage' hint is gone.

features.name: Per-line AI price read and hard-filtered comps
features.description: Prompt 70 (built directly from the prompt-69 spec's locked scope; no standalone spec file was written). The comps engine is HARD-FILTERED on system type: buildComps' ladder is exact -> same-system any-size -> none, and it never crosses systems (the old widen ladder dropped the system filter under 3 same-system jobs, which is why AI suggestions read as square-foot-only; a quartz price built from polyaspartic comps is worse than no comp at all). The AI price read moved from one job-level recommendation to ONE model call returning a recommendation PER LINE plus a short job-level roll-up whose range is the SUM of the line ranges (server-derived). Each line carries a range, a why, and a SERVER-computed confidence flag (comps_backed / thin_sample / no_comps, from its own comps sample vs comps_min_sample), never model-claimed; the model's claims are overwritten. Custom lines reason from their typed scope and their why carries an explicit no-comparables statement, enforced deterministically in production/ai-lines.cjs. The inputs key is per-line (system+sqft+mvb for calc lines; typed price + scope hash for custom lines, joined in order) so reopening an unchanged estimate stays a zero-cost cache hit; pricing_snapshot.ai.lines[].line_key is the per-line keying the prompt-69 seam reserved, while the snapshot's top-level shape is unchanged. Settings > Estimates > Pricing intelligence: estimate_ai_enabled (clean disabled state, never an error) and comps_min_sample (the ONE knob the ladder and the confidence flag share). Legacy single-recommendation request bodies still work (deploy-skew safety), and pre-70 snapshots still render on the estimate detail page.

other: production/ai-lines.cjs (new: confidence, inputs key, prompt, parse/finalize)

features.spec: claude-code-prompt-69-per-line-pricing-custom-lines.md (the 'Explicitly out of scope' section defines prompt 70)

features.name: Optional line items on any line
features.description: Prompt 72: any estimate line (calculator area, custom line, add-on) can be marked optional for the customer, with ONE structural floor: an estimate cannot be SENT with zero required lines (gated in the dashboard send email/text/present flows via estimateOptionalGateOk), which is what makes the customer floor automatic since required lines render with NO checkbox at all. Optional AREA and CUSTOM lines start TICKED (opt-out, 'Starts selected for the customer', default from optional_lines_preselect_default); add-ons keep their opt-in behavior. estimate_areas.is_optional/preselected are the source of truth (the estimator reloads areas by position) and mirror onto estimate_line_items at save. Two stored numbers: estimates.price = required-only floor while open (every stored GP bucket follows the same set) and price_all_options = the ceiling; the pipeline and list render '$X (up to $Y)' only while open and different; the send email quotes the OPENING total (required + pre-selected) computed live from the rows so it matches the page. The public page renders 'Your project' (required, no control, plus pre-selected optional lines with a ticked toggle and an Optional tag) and 'Options to add' (unselected), and a crafted zero-selection accept returns 400 before the status CAS. On accept the job is built from SELECTED areas only: job_areas, pec_prod_areas (the recipe side, so the material plan/ordering/costing re-cost on what was actually sold, deliberately NOT a price change), jobs.sqft, jobs.scope and pec_prod_jobs.notes (selected lines' scope + a 'Declined by customer: ...' line; byte-identical when nothing declined; an area with NO line item is structurally KEPT). estimates.scope_of_work is never rewritten after signature. Declined lines (is_optional AND NOT selected) are the record: struck through + Declined on the estimate detail, listed on a job 'Declined options' card with one-click Add to job (change-order modal prefilled at the ORIGINALLY quoted price, materials re-cost at current catalog; custom declined lines prefill Simple mode since they have no recipe), and one line each on the customer card. No automation fires on a decline. The required-only GP amber warning (optional_lines_gp_warn_pct) warns, never blocks. Settings > Estimates > Optional lines; optional_lines_enabled is a CREATE gate, never a data-hiding gate. Shared rules live in production/optional-lines.cjs (estimator + pec-public-estimate.cjs + 45 fixture checks). Prompt 78: customer ticks are saved onto the rows as they happen (debounced 250ms 'select' POST, fire-and-forget; the signature freeze at accept remains the authority) and price settles when the accept panel first opens, not on every tick. scopeSendBlockers/estimateSendGateOk also hard-block unfilled placeholders on EVERY line description plus estimates.scope_of_work: the literal BLANK (case sensitive), unresolved is/is not choices, and ___ fill-in runs (production/scope.cjs scopeBlanks, mirrored client-side as estScopeBlanks). Custom lines stay exempt from the empty-description rule but their typed blanks block. The old estimateBlankScopeOk warn-and-allow confirm is deleted; hard block, no override, no settings key (rule 12 waived by decision).

features.name: Crew notes on the work order
features.description: A short internal brief for the install crew (cliff notes on what the job is, plus watch-outs like access, prep, and site conditions), separate from the customer scope. Typed on the estimator in either mode or AI-drafted from the proposal with a manual Generate from proposal button (undoable, edits always win, never invents facts not in the estimate). It carries to the job on accept, stays editable on the job page's Job Card block, and prints in its own Crew Notes section on the crew work order. Strictly internal: it never appears on the customer proposal, estimate page, portal, or PDF. Prompt 55: the work order's Job Identity grid carries a Salesperson pair (fills the grid's former empty slot, so row count and the prompt-53 header height math are untouched); blank prints Unassigned, deliberately unlike the handwritten CREW/DATE hero boxes.

features.name: Live proposal panel
features.description: The customer-facing proposal builds live inside the estimator as reps work, drafting from scope templates the moment an area has a system and square footage. The AI writes the polished version automatically on the first save once scope questions are answered, then only rewrites on an explicit Regenerate, and reps can edit the text in place before sending.

features.name: Structured customer and address fields
features.description: The estimator's customer card starts with a Residential or Commercial choice, capturing first/last name or company name plus optional contact, and splits the address into real fields. With a Google key configured, typing a street suggests real addresses and fills city, state, and zip, while everything stays hand-editable and fully offline. Commercial estimates carry the company name onto the proposal and the customer record. 2026-08-10: the customer card moved from the left column to a full-width header above the two columns. Once the info is inputted (same completeness rule as the save gate) it locks into a compact summary bar (name, Residential/Commercial tag, phone, email, address); clicking the bar reopens the editable card, Done re-locks, and picking a duplicate-search match auto-locks.

features.name: Sales Pipeline board
features.description: A Kanban Sales Pipeline board (rail group Sales Pipeline, item Pipeline; individual records are still Leads) shows every lead as a card across seven pre-sale stages from New to Accepted or Lost, with drag-to-advance, per-column counts and pipeline value, source/campaign/owner filters, and speed-to-lead timers that turn red after an hour so no lead sits unclaimed. The Estimate Scheduled stage (third, between Contacted and Estimate Sent) fills itself when an on-site estimate appointment is booked (client Schedule Estimate flow or Routemize intake; a NEW lead entering it also stamps contacted_at) and empties back to Contacted when the last scheduled estimate is canceled; its cards carry an appointment date chip and the column sorts soonest visit first. Each card carries a Contacted Nx chip derived read-only from the outbound comms logs plus drip sends (calls, texts, emails matched by customer_id then normalized phone; drip ledger rows attributed by lead_id, with the drip mirror rows in the comms logs excluded so nothing double-counts; 0 reads Not contacted, red on an aging new lead) and a Hot/Warm/Cold AI score badge (70/40 cutoffs) with a hot-first sort in the filter bar. Facebook and Google form leads land in HQ automatically with an instant AI summary, 1-100 score, and next step, and duplicate submissions fold into the existing lead. Cards with an active drip enrollment show a small Drip chip. Prompt 61 (Parts D-E): leads.source and customers.lead_source now share ONE vocabulary, the managed pec_lead_sources names (aliases column maps raw feed tokens at intake via resolveLeadSourceName, editable in Settings > Lead sources); badge color/label lookups normalize through leadSourceKey so canonical names stay colored. The source is manually editable on the lead detail (click the badge) and the customer detail (click the source line), the two stay in sync, and every change writes a source_changed lead_events row with the actor. No permission gate, no bulk edit, no kanban-card editor, all by explicit decision. Prompt 62: a derived Drafts column (estimates with status draft and no sent_at; NOT a leads.stage value) sits between Estimate Scheduled and Estimate Sent, and the board renders TWO card shapes: lead cards (now with a Draft chip when a draft estimate rides them, and a Contact line for business leads) plus estimate cards for estimates with no lead, which move by the estimate's own status and cannot be dragged (dropping a lead on Drafts explains itself). Counts, value rollups, search and date filters handle both shapes; source/campaign/owner filters exclude estimate cards; the Drafts footer shows a count when every card is priceless. Leads can be ARCHIVED off the board (archived_at; stage untouched, drips stopped three ways, contact kept) behind a Show: Archived filter, and the New lead modal uses the Individual/Business name model (first+last OR business_name always required, full_name stays the derived display column). Prompt 75: cards carry a proposal-view corner chip, an eye icon with the open count that becomes a flame when the shared hot rule is met (estimate_hot_min_views/estimate_hot_window_hours in Settings > Estimates); it appears on no-lead estimate cards and on lead cards whose latest estimate was sent, loads in one aggregate query inside loadLeadsData, and is deliberately distinct from the AI Hot/Warm/Cold lead-score badge (lead quality vs the customer reading the proposal right now).

features.name: Lead drip engine
features.description: Automatic AI-tailored follow-up drips for leads: new leads auto-enroll (intake webhook and manual add) in a seeded 30-day 8-step taper (days 1,2,4,7,11,16,22,30, SMS/email/both per step). A scheduled runner (every 15 min) re-checks four kill-switches at send time (lead replied via inbound text/call, stage advanced past contacted or lost, opted out, max touches), defers SMS outside 8am-8pm Phoenix, renders each message per lead with Claude (no invented facts, no em dashes, no links; scrubber enforces), and sends through the same Quo/Resend request shapes as the manual senders, mirroring rows into pec_sms_log (kind drip) / pec_email_log (template_key drip). Safety: global master switch (settings key drip_sending_enabled, ships OFF), per-campaign dry_run mode (default; writes review copy, never sends), claim-first concurrency (no double-send possible), first SMS carries Reply STOP to opt out, Quo STOP flips leads.opted_out and stops the enrollment. Admin Drips view (master switch, mode/pause toggles, steps, recent activity); lead detail shows a Drip card with Stop/Enroll and the messages in the timeline. Phase 3 generalized the engine to SUBJECTS: enrollments carry subject_type (lead or job) plus subject_id, one active enrollment per subject per campaign (a lead can hold a lead-nurture drip and an estimate drip at once, never two of the same), a recipient resolver maps a subject to its contact + consent model (lead = positive sms_consent; job = the customer's opt-out-only sms_opt_out), and kill-switches run a universal core plus a per-kind adapter. See the Estimate follow-up drip, Invoice payment reminders, and Review request drip entries for the other kinds; the review kind (prompt 60) is the fourth, and the only one that shipped mode='live' behind the approval gate instead of dry_run, with its own enroll-time gate guard, its own master switch (review_drip_enabled), and per-kind stop conditions (reviewed / touchup_opened / job_closed / bad_review). Prompt 42 (go-live prep) added a GLOBAL approval gate: while the settings key drip_approval_required is 'true', a due step on a LIVE campaign renders its real copy into a 'pending' pec_drip_sends row (one per sendable leg, held once per step by a partial unique index) and the enrollment does NOT advance until a human approves, edits, or skips it in the Drip Approvals view; approving re-runs consent + kill-switches + quiet hours at that moment (a reply/STOP/payment/lost between render and approve voids the item with the reason shown), sends through the same providers, and advances with the same claim. SMS approved outside the window sits as 'queued' and is flushed by the runner at the window open with a final consent re-check. Quiet hours are settings-driven (drip_quiet_start/end/days, default 08:00-20:00 Phoenix Mon-Sat) and editable in Settings > Drips along with the master switch and the gate. Prompt 73 (2026-08-06): the taper became 9 steps with a NEW day-0 instant touch. A lead arriving through the pec-lead-intake webhook (any online lead) gets ONE fixed-template thank-you message inline in the same request (sendInstantTouch in _pec-drip.cjs): email always, SMS only with positive consent (a skipped ledger row records no_sms_consent so gaps are explained). It is the only step with auto_send=true and a fixed_template, so it bypasses ONLY the approval gate and quiet hours; the kill switch, master switch, consent, opt-out, and archived checks all still apply, and steps 1-8 keep the full gate. Concurrency is claim-first (the conditional next_step_index 0->1 advance), so a Zapier retry or a racing runner tick can never double-send; the runner's own auto_send branch is the crash safety net. A {booking_link} token (settings key routemize_booking_url, Settings > Drips) renders into the day-0 template via a {{#booking_link}} conditional block (empty URL drops the whole sentence) and is offered to the AI steps 1-8 through the render prompt; renderCopyReal rejects any rendered routemize.com URL that is not character-identical to the configured one, and scrubCopyKeepUrl lets exactly that one URL through the scrubber. Cancel/no-show re-engagement: a Routemize cancellation with no other live appointment re-enrolls a new/contacted lead starting at STEP 1 (never the day-0 auto-reply). scripts/enroll-lead-backlog.cjs (gated, --dry-run first) enrolls the pre-73 backlog at step 1 with the same exclusions. Master switch for the whole day-0 behavior: drip_instant_touch_enabled (Settings > Drips). Prompt 81: dripEmailHtml renders the code-appended estimate/pay/review tails as a lead-in sentence plus a centered accent button (accent from pec_brand_identity via getBrandAccent, memoized per function instance); the pec_drip_sends ledger and the SMS leg keep the plain-text URL verbatim, and an approval-edited tail that no longer matches the pattern falls back to a plain link.

features.name: Estimate follow-up drip
features.description: When an estimate is sent to the customer, the lead automatically moves from the lead-nurture drip to an estimate follow-up drip (the nurture drip stops with reason estimate_sent so nobody is on two tracks). Taper: days 1, 3, 7, 14 after the send, AI-written warm nudges to review and sign. The message may state the estimate price only when the record carries one, and the real signing link (/e/token) is appended by code after the AI scrub, so the model can never invent a link or amount. Stops at send time when any of the lead's estimates is accepted or signed (the interim signed state counts), when all are rejected or the lead is lost, on a portal change request (counts as replied, a human takes over), on an inbound text or call, on opt-out, or at max touches. Re-sending a revised estimate after a stop starts a fresh taper. Runs on the shared drip engine (master switch + dry_run rules apply); campaign ships dry_run.

features.name: Invoice payment reminders
features.description: Automatic payment reminders for open invoices. The first time an invoice goes to the customer (email compose or the Text invoice button; both stamp jobs.invoice_first_sent_at first-send-wins) the JOB enrolls in a reminder drip: day 0, then +3, +7, +14, anchored to the send moment. Invoice terms (2026-08-17): a job with a FUTURE jobs.invoice_due_date and no payment schedule holds instead of sending, and the enrollment re-anchors to the due-date morning, so a Net 30 customer is reminded at due+0/+3/+7/+14, never dunned on day 3. Every run the engine recomputes the real balance from jobs.price minus pec_payments; a partial payment keeps the reminders coming showing the remaining balance, and the payment that clears it stops the enrollment with reason paid on the next tick. The recipient is the job's customer; their STOP (sms_opt_out) silences the SMS leg while email reminders continue, and an inbound text or call stops the whole drip as replied. Balance and pay link (/pay/token) are appended by code, never written by the model. Voided or archived jobs stop as job_closed. Money guardrail: the campaign ships dry_run and stays there until Dylan reviews generated copy and flips it live himself. Prompt 45: when the job has a payment schedule, reminders state the current outstanding ask (deposit or installment, with its label) instead of the full balance, and stop as not_due while nothing is currently due.

features.name: Manual blast tool
features.description: One composed message to a filtered audience, sent from the Drips page via a 3-step wizard: compose (one shared SMS and/or email; {first_name} is the only personalization; an optional Draft with AI button drafts from a typed goal and can never invent offers the goal does not state), audience (filter leads by stage/source/campaign/brand and customers by tag/company, then deselect anyone; opt-outs and missing consent are hard-filtered BEFORE the count is shown with removed counts displayed, and recipients are de-duped by phone/email with leads winning collisions), and a confirm step stating the EXACT per-channel counts that nothing sends without. Recipients are materialized as queued rows in the shared pec_drip_sends ledger (blast_id set); the drain claims each row conditionally (queued -> sending -> sent/failed), re-checks consent at send time so a late STOP wins, holds SMS outside 8am-8pm Phoenix, and is resumable and double-send-proof by construction. pec-blast-run kicks immediate sending after confirm; the 15-minute drip tick is the safety net. The master switch gates blasts too. Every text carries Reply STOP to opt out; lead-directed blast sends count as outbound touches via the shared ledger. Prompt 81: a blast body that ends with its only URL gets that URL promoted to a centered accent button in the email render (two or more URLs stay inline so buttons never stack mid-blast); the queued ledger body stays plain text.

features.name: Drip and blast performance metrics
features.description: Two Sales-section Metrics cards (the former Phase 3 placeholder slot). Drip performance: one row per sequence kind (lead nurture, estimate follow-up, invoice reminders) with its dry-run/LIVE chip, active enrollments right now, sends and dry-run previews in the window, replies, and conversions (stage advanced / signed / paid) with a conversion rate over enrollments that ended in the window, plus a stop-reason bar chart and a drill to the window's sends. Blast performance: recent blasts with sent/failed/skipped, opt-outs generated after confirm, per-blast drills, and a weekly sent-volume chart; notes honestly that blast replies are not machine-attributed. Both filter by the existing Metrics time window, degrade to a not-migrated notice pre-migration, and show honest empty states while data is thin.

features.name: Drip approval gate and settings controls
features.description: The supervised-launch layer over the drip engine (prompt 42). Drip Approvals (admin nav) lists every held drip message across leads and jobs, newest first: recipient with masked phone/email, campaign + step, and the editable body (plus subject for email). Per item: Approve & Send (re-checks consent, opt-out, replies, stage/paid/lost, and quiet hours at that exact moment, then sends via the normal providers, logs 'sent', and advances the enrollment exactly like an auto-send), Skip this step (advances without sending), Stop drip (ends the enrollment). Settings > Drips holds the knobs, all settings-table rows per standing rule 12: the master sending switch (same drip_sending_enabled row as the Drips view, so the two mirror each other), the approval gate (drip_approval_required; ON for the launch week, Dylan flips it off for full-auto), and the SMS send window (drip_quiet_start/drip_quiet_end/drip_quiet_days, Arizona time; texts due outside it wait for the next open, emails send any time, and the window also governs blasts). The gate intercepts LIVE campaigns only (dry-run already sends nothing); a leftover pending item keeps its step held even after the gate is switched off, so flipping the gate can never auto-send something a human was reviewing. The Approvals page also hosts the Invoice installments queue (prompt 45; see Deposits and payment schedules). Prompt 73: the gate gained ONE per-step exception, auto_send (today only the lead campaign's day-0 fixed-template instant touch). auto_send lives on the step row, never in settings, so no toggle can ever auto-send the AI-written steps; the pending-hold branch (a step a human is mid-review on) still outranks it.

features.name: Lead detail with AI game plan
features.description: Clicking a lead opens its full page: contact info, an Outreach line (times contacted broken down by calls/texts/emails/drip messages with the last touch, derived from the outbound comms logs and the drip send ledger), notes, and activity timeline on one side, and an AI read on the other with the Hot/Warm/Cold score badge (also shown beside the name up top with the AI's one-line reason), the single best next step, call talking points, and ready-to-copy text and email drafts. Stage changes, note edits, analysis refresh, and Start estimate (which opens the estimator already tied to the lead) all live on the page, and once OpenPhone is connected calls and transcripts appear in the timeline automatically. A Drip section shows the enrollment (active step / stopped reason) with Stop and Enroll buttons, the messages already sent or held (full body behind expandable rows, with a Review shortcut to Drip Approvals when something is waiting), and the UPCOMING steps with their planned dates, so the card answers what is coming next, not just what already went out. Drip messages also appear in the Activity timeline. Prompt 62: an Edit name modal (Individual/Business, same rules as the customer form), an Archive/Unarchive toolbar action with an archived banner, lost notes shown under the lost reason, and the Mark-lost modal gained an always-available optional notes box plus an AI suggestion pre-filled from the lead's most recent call (matched via customer_id or last-10 phone digits against pec_call_log, which has no lead_id); Other now stores 'Other' with the text in lost_notes.

features.name: Customers and jobs records
features.description: The core CRM record set: a searchable customer list with structured residential/commercial fields, lead sources, and tags, and a jobs list and pipeline board where each job opens to a redesigned detail page with a line-items estimate table, change-order boxes, notes, job-card fields, price per square foot, and a sticky save bar. Includes CSV customer import in the DripJobs export shape. Prompt 55: jobs.salesperson (frozen from the estimate on accept) is the single display source for who sold the job; the job header shows it (blank = Unassigned), only an admin can change it inline, and a change mirrors to pec_prod_jobs.sales_team over the deal-id bridge and lands in the job activity log. Prompt 63 (Part B, verified not built): the job detail's Line Items editor IS where colors and products get chosen after the sale (per-recipe-slot picks incl. the flake swatch grid, saved to job_area_materials + legacy job_areas mirrors via pec_replace_job_areas); picks feed ordering (computeMaterialPlan / resolveJobLines) and the printed work order but NEVER money, since jobs.price/line_items derive from typed per-area prices and costing reads its own cost snapshots (guard comment at the saveJob write site). 2026-08-10: the job detail's Colors card grew an inline flake-color editor (input with a datalist of active flake blends) that writes the SAME estimates.flake_color field the estimate page edits, so the color can be set without opening the estimate; saving a non-empty color also marks colors confirmed in the same click (picking the color IS the confirmation). Lightweight immediate write, never the big Save. Cross-nav (2026-08-10): the job detail toolbar shows View Estimate (from the batched reverse query estimates.job_id=eq.<job>, newest wins; hidden for manual/DripJobs jobs with no estimate).

features.name: Unified Messages inbox
features.description: A Messages tab that merges texts and call logs into one conversation per phone number, newest first, with All/Texts/Calls filters. Every conversation is clickable and replyable, even unknown numbers, which can be attached to a customer (filing all their texts and calls) or turned into a new lead with the phone prefilled. Prompt 38: customer phone numbers render with tap-to-call plus a Text action on the job detail header (routes to that job's comms tab), the lead card and lead detail, the appointment popup, and the printed crew work order; the Text action opens the existing Messages thread (openMessageThread now seeds an empty thread for a number with no history), so consent/STOP and logging stay in this one surface.

features.name: Messages & Calls on the job
features.description: Every job and customer profile has a phone-app-style feed showing the customer's texts and phone calls together in time order, with chat bubbles, call cards, AI call summaries, and full transcripts. Staff text the customer right from the job, and the same feed powers invoice and estimate conversations.

features.name: Job Schedule calendar
features.description: A rolling Week / 3-week production calendar with continuous multi-day job bars, color coded by system, per-week prorated revenue that opens a click-through breakdown, and short per-segment notes (like flake portion) on the bars. Jobs carry their system automatically from the accepted estimate, days are numbered chronologically, and the pending-jobs panel offers quick read-only job details and sizes itself to the calendar. It reflows into a tappable day list on phones. The +Schedule modal also shows the job's CompanyCam site photos read-only (reads jobs.companycam_project_id via the dripjobs_deal_id bridge through the pec-companycam proxy), and both month day pickers ring today's date. Prompt 51: the left aside is now a column holding the Touch-ups panel (see 'Touch-up list and callback tracking') above Pending Jobs, and BOTH pending sources exclude is_callback rows, so an unscheduled touch-up never renders as an ordinary pending job card. The week-revenue exclusion now tests revenue, not the flag: a billable callback (revenue > 0) prorates like any job. Prompt 54: crews themselves stay pec_prod_crews (a crew is a grouping, not a person); people are assigned to crews from Settings > People, writing pec_prod_crew_members.crew_id. Prompt 55: the schedule surfaces (modal, Pending cards, read-only popup, calendar bars, Next Day board + run sheet) autofill system type and estimated hours from the ESTIMATE via one shared helper (prodJobEstimateFacts, backed by buildProdEstimateFacts, the extracted loadCostingData estimate phase), so they always match the Budget card and Job Costing. System: a real pec_prod_areas system (an explicit modal pick) wins; else the estimate-derived system follows live. Hours: a typed override (pec_prod_jobs.estimated_hours) wins on schedule surfaces only; else the computed budgetedHours; costing/bonus keep using the computed number per prompt 50. The modal writes estimated_hours only when the field differs from its prefill, and shows an 'Estimate now says N hrs' drift line with one-click adoption. Prompt 57: bars are FILLED by crew color (pec_prod_crews.color, picked in the crew modal with presets) with the system type as a thin top band (--ev-banner pseudo-element); a crew color key renders above the calendar and a crew with no color falls back to the system fill. Callbacks keep sky blue with no crew fill. Clicking a bar opens the READ-ONLY quick look (openJobQuickLook); the Schedule button inside it is the only path to the edit modal. Sq footage rides the bar tooltip via prodJobEstimateFacts.sqft (jobEffectiveSqft: manual jobs.sqft, else the area sum), the same number Job Costing shows. Prompt 58: every calendar grid is Sunday-first (startOfWeek flipped; per-week revenue re-buckets at the new boundary), and every schedule surface shows a DERIVED price via prodJobDisplayRevenue: the CRM jobs.price (estimate lines + change orders) when the prod job resolves to a CRM card, else the stored pec_prod_jobs.revenue, with stored winning for callbacks, finalized/completed jobs, and $0-estimate cards. The stored revenue is never rewritten; the schedule modal shows the derived number read-only with the booked-at delta, and manual jobs keep the editable field. 2026-08-10: saving a schedule (both the Schedule modal and + Add Job) now returns the calendar to TODAY's week instead of pinning it to the earliest selected day, which for a rescheduled job was its ORIGINAL date and yanked the view back weeks.

features.name: Touch-up list and callback tracking
features.description: A Touch-ups panel in the Job Schedule aside (above Pending Jobs) that tracks every touch-up / warranty callback from request to close. A touch-up stays a full callback job (pec_prod_jobs, is_callback + original_job_id); the panel adds a lifecycle (touchup_state: open / scheduled / waiting_customer / done, a parallel axis to status, which callbacks keep at 'unscheduled'), an age clock (touchup_opened_at; rows go red past touchup_aging_days), manual drag order (touchup_order) with an optional deterministic Sort by suggested (+40 active customer job, +25 crew in the same city in the visible window, +days open capped at 30, -15 waiting; Undo restores touchup_order_prev), and a close flow that REQUIRES a cause from a six-value enum ('other' requires a note) and never deletes anything. Intake is office-only from two places: the panel's + Touch-up (search past jobs by name/address, description + touchup_requested_by) and the job detail toolbar's + Touch-up (prod row resolved by deal id then jobNameAddrKey); both flow through addTouchupCallback (the legacy #schedAddCallback button keeps its confirm + straight-to-scheduler path). Text opens the original job's comms tab with a prefilled draft (one-shot window.__pecCommsPrefill). Billable override: touchup_billable + revenue save together from the schedule modal; the four revenue-exclusion sites test revenue (a null-revenue callback stays $0). The panel's Report modal totals closed touch-ups by cause and by the ORIGINAL job's crew (90 days / YTD) with a callback rate. Callback costs roll up read-only into the parent's unified costing GP display without touching computeCrewBonus inputs (prompt 50's review gate stays the only bonus lever). Prompt 58: the collapsed panel header counts open + scheduled together as 'outstanding' (everything not done), while the Ops Queue check still deliberately counts only unactioned open touch-ups.

features.name: Reschedule / pending flow
features.description: When a job or part of one gets bumped, staff pull specific days off the calendar and the job parks in the Pending column with an amber reschedule badge showing days owed and the date pulled, keeping crew, hours, and price intact until it is rebooked. Calendar tasks, holidays, and days off slot alongside jobs. Clicking a pending job's name or card opens the read-only quick look. Prompt 57: openPendingJobCard was renamed openJobQuickLook and enriched (crew, scheduled date range with day count, customer phone tel: link from the CRM bridge, material picks, TOUCHUP badge); every schedule surface now opens it.

features.name: Next Day Schedule and run sheet
features.description: A focused next-working-day view that lays out each crew's jobs for tomorrow with prorated revenue, plus a Print run sheet button that produces a paper crew sheet. A big job can be split across two crews so it appears under both crew columns in the same slot with a 2 teams badge and on the printed sheet, while staying one job for revenue and status. It stacks into full-width mobile cards. Clicking a job's name on a run-sheet card opens the read-only quick look; dragging the card still moves it between crews and slots. Prompt 51: scheduled touch-ups appear in the crew's column badged TOUCHUP (sky blue, the calendar's callback color) with their description, and print on the run sheet with a plain-text ' - TOUCHUP' marker plus the description line; revenue stays $0 unless the touch-up is billable. The day-revenue total excludes only NO-revenue callbacks. Prompt 57: the WHOLE card opens the read-only quick look (drag-to-move preserved via a dragstart flag plus a pointer-distance guard); cards and the printed sheet carry a crew-color left edge with a system-color top band and show sq footage from the shared prodJobEstimateFacts helper.

features.name: Material ordering
features.description: A job-first Ordering view: a Jobs-to-order list of open jobs with schedule dates, crew, system, colors-confirmed and material-status chips, where you hand-pick the jobs to order for; the Order sheet aggregates the selected jobs by supplier with per-line editable order quantities that persist as manual overrides (order_qty_manual, kept through Recalculate until reset), ordered check-offs, hand-added lines (manual_added), and a print mode. Recalculate merges instead of clobbering (mergeRecalcLines). A by-customer putaway list and the date-range Pull Material modal remain. Ordering is gated behind a colors-confirmed check, surfaced as a disabled checkbox instead of a silent skip. Prompt 75: change-order areas never auto-generate material lines (crmPlanAreas drops is_change_order rows; a job whose only areas are change orders shows an explicit skip reason); a blank cure speed inherits the job's dominant one at plan-input time (inheritCureSpeeds) so same-product lines merge instead of splitting on the product|cure SKU key; a swatch area with no blend picked renders a zero-quantity 'Flake color not chosen' row that can never be ordered or persisted, plus a warning chip on the Jobs-to-order row; skip reasons render on the job row; and a Refresh button plus a 5-minute visibilitychange reload cover the page's reload-on-entry-only staleness gap.

features.name: Price & Material Catalog
features.description: The single catalog of products, materials, flake colors, add-ons, and system-type recipes with pricing that feeds estimating, ordering, and costing. Products carry an explicit cost basis (per gallon/box/pack versus per kit, auto-converted by kit size), each flake carries its own default basecoat, systems show a collapsible one-line recipe summary, and material categories include liquids, flake, quartz, and Polycoat. Admins tune per-system target gross profit and the sundries rate here. Prompt 53: each product can carry two uploaded PDFs, a data sheet (TDS) and an MSDS/SDS, stored as object paths in the public pec-datasheets Supabase Storage bucket (the app's first Storage feature); the list shows TDS/SDS chips and the editor uploads on file pick under a random UUID name so an unsaved product can carry a file. Prompt 57 (pending the 2026-07-29_flake_color_model.sql migration): the 18 identically priced Torginol flake products condense into ONE Standard Flake product and the BLEND moves to the colors table (category='flake-blend', 21 rows carrying product_id + default_basecoat_product_id + active). The New Job flake picker lists colors and writes flake_color_id + flake_product_id together; basecoat resolves explicit pick > the color's pairing > the product's pairing (legacy rows) > slot default (flakeColorBasecoatDefaults beside flakeBasecoatDefaults). Obsidian, Autumn Brown, and Stonewash keep their own products (different cost or spread rate); the retired 18 are DEACTIVATED, never deleted (historical areas FK to them), hidden behind the catalog's new Show inactive toggle. flakeProductSaveError exempts color='Per-job pick' products from the mandatory-basecoat gate. Pre-migration everything renders exactly as before (colorMode detection).

features.name: Product data sheets (TDS / MSDS)
features.description: Two PDFs per catalog product, a technical data sheet (TDS) and an MSDS/SDS, uploaded from the product editor into the PUBLIC pec-datasheets Supabase Storage bucket (public by decision: crews have no login, and a public URL survives being printed or texted). Rows store the storage object PATH, never a URL; the browser builds links with getPublicUrl. Uploads happen on file pick (object named crypto.randomUUID() + '.pdf'), Save persists the paths, and replaced/removed objects are deleted only after a successful save so a saved row never points at a deleted file. The catalog list shows clickable TDS/SDS chips (dimmed when missing), and the job detail header shows a Data sheets button ONLY when a product in the job's material plan has a sheet, opening a modal of every sheet for the job (material resolution shared with the printed work order via computeJobMaterialLines). Max upload size is the datasheet_max_upload_mb setting (Settings > General); the bucket enforces 10 MB + PDF-only server-side.

features.name: Job costing
features.description: Where a completed job's real costs, materials used, crew hours, and revenue are entered to calculate gross profit, GP/hr, REV/hr, price per square foot (manual job sqft when there are no areas, e.g. custom jobs), and the crew bonus pool. It derives materials from the job card when production lines are empty, supports ad-hoc material lines and editable revenue, and includes a live search across active and completed costings. Prompt 50: the unified detail is an accordion (always-visible profit summary card, collapsible Revenue & Job Info / Labor & Bonus Payout / Materials / Subcontractors / Crew Bonuses / Costs / Notes sections, session-remembered via _unifiedSecOpen, layout only), and the Notes section carries an Office notes box (office_notes/_by/_at on pec_prod_job_costing, saved via saveOfficeNotes with an author+time stamp, separate from the crew-adjacent notes column). openCostingDetail is the superseded modal with no remaining callers. Prompt 51: a parent job's unified detail folds every child touch-up's totalVar into its displayed Total Var and GP via a read-only Callback costs line in the Costs section (clickable through to each touch-up's own costing). Display-layer only: computeCostingRow is untouched, so aggregateCostingRows / Metrics sums count each job's costs once and never double count. Prompt 52: actual crew hours come from the imported BusyBusy Payroll Export rows (wage_type OT1 rows are the OT slice; rows with an unmapped or ignored name never count); a job with imported rows uses them and shows its manual hours greyed for reference, and a finalized job whose live hours drift from the recorded hours_actual snapshot shows a display-only 'Hours changed since finalize' note (the import never writes to bonus tables). Prompt 56: crew labor finally hits GP. loadCostingData reads the BusyBusy mirror once and bbAccumulateEntries builds state.bbHoursByJobMember; crewLaborForJob turns it (BusyBusy first, manual per-member hours second) into ONE loaded labor cost via computeCrewBonus.actualLabor, and costingDerivedForJob feeds it to computeCostingRow's new trailing derived arg ({ laborCost, actHrs, pendingBonus }) on the detail, the callback rollup, the finalized list + Rollups, and Metrics. Salary & Wages renders derived (read-only, hours + wages + burden note; a hand-typed value stays visible as unused), the Hrs column and GP/hr populate from crew hours, and a suggested-but-unapproved bonus counts against GP as pending (pendingBonusForJob returns 0 once a Labor-savings ledger row exists, so approval never double-counts). The Crew Bonuses accordion section was removed (the free-form + Add bonus row path is gone); the $50 crew lead checkbox and a read-only Recorded bonuses list live on the Labor & Bonus Payout card. Kill switches: costing_labor_from_hours (rollback to stored fields) and costing_count_pending_bonus. Prompt-56 STOP resolved (Dylan, 2026-07-29, option C): the manual per-member hours fallback derives labor ONLY when no Salary & Wages was hand-typed, freezing the 34 legacy jobs (31 finalized) whose typed labor the fallback had silently overridden; BusyBusy hours still beat a typed value. Metrics applies the same rule. Prompt 66: computeCostingRow's GP math is extracted to production/costing.js (pure ESM, test-covered); index.html keeps a byte-identical mirror (calculator.js convention) with the shared estimate injected via costingDerivedForJob, numeric behavior unchanged.

features.name: Costing submit-for-review approval
features.description: Non-admin office staff submit a finished costing for review, which locks the numbers, and an admin finalizes it from a Submitted-for-review queue. Admins can send a costing back with a required reason that reaches the submitter three ways (a banner on the job, a bell notification, and a Slack message) and is kept as a history, and finalizing opens a per-member bonus approval step showing each crew member's suggested bonus for adjustment before it is recorded with a full audit trail. Prompt 56: approving the crew bonus is its own one-click button on the Labor & Bonus Payout card (suggested amount exactly, no per-member editing; writeLaborSavingsLedger is the single ledger write path shared with Finalize, incl. the pre-migration audit-column retry). When a job's bonus is already approved, the finalize dialog shows the recorded rows read-only and leaves them untouched, so approved_by/approved_at are never overwritten by the finalizer; Unapprove deletes only the Labor-savings rows.

features.name: Crew bonus and Bonus Report
features.description: Crew bonuses are computed from the labor budget minus actual loaded labor using per-member wages set in Settings, recorded to a ledger on finalize, and tracked as paid or pending in a Bonus Report. Branded one-page print/PDF payout handout sheets can be generated per crew member. Prompt 50 Part E: a bonus becomes payable only bonus_lock_days (default 14) days after the job's completion date on public.jobs.completed_date, bridged from pec_prod_jobs by dripjobs_deal_id then name+address (jobNameAddrKey); a missing completion date reads as LOCKED with a Set completion date affordance, never unlocked. A callback (is_callback + original_job_id) flags the parent job's bonuses for manual review (Pay full / Reduce / Void with review_status/reviewed_by/reviewed_at/review_note; unreviewed = not payable). Paid payouts can be Reversed (admin-only, matching the bp_write is_admin_role() policy): reversed_at/_by/_reason mark the row, it stops counting as paid in every sum and on handouts, and nothing is ever deleted. Prompt 51: the callback cost rollup on the parent's costing is GP display only and does NOT change computeCrewBonus inputs, so the bonus pool on a parent with callbacks is numerically unchanged; the prompt-50 review gate stays the single lever on bonus. Prompt 52: actual hours now come from the BusyBusy Payroll Export import (BusyBusy wins over manual entry when a job has imported rows); OT is BusyBusy's weekly-40 attribution accepted deliberately (the premium lands on whatever job the person was on at hour 40, Dylan's documented tradeoff), and the import never writes to pec_prod_job_bonuses or pec_bonus_payouts. Prompt 54: pec_prod_crew_members rows (ids and hourly_wage) are unchanged and remain the wage source, but they are now mirrored from public.people; wages are editable from Settings > People as well as the legacy Team Members card, both writing the same rows. Prompt 56: the four formula constants are settings-backed (bonus_crew_fraction_pct, bonus_labor_burden_pct, bonus_ot_multiplier, costing_default_labor_budget_pct; shipped values stay the fallback, hydrated by applyCostingBonusSettings from the loaders' existing settings reads) under Settings > General > Job Costing & Bonus. The same computeCrewBonus actualLabor is now the job's Salary & Wages cost everywhere via crewLaborForJob, so the labor line and the bonus math structurally cannot disagree. saveBonusField/addBonusRow (the free-form editable bonus rows) were removed with the Crew Bonuses card.

features.name: Commission tracking
features.description: A Commission view showing per-salesperson commission as a rate-derived cost baked into the price, with payouts driven off the payment-received date on a Sunday-Saturday period with a Friday payroll check date. Owner-sold jobs are excluded via a per-seller flag, each commission clicks through to its job, and results filter by date range and salesperson. Prompt 54: rates still come from pec_sales_team_members, but pctByName and the exclusion set now also resolve name_aliases (former names captured automatically on any rename by a trigger on pec_sales_team_members), so renaming a rep in the People directory or anywhere else can never silently detach historical pec_job_ar salesperson strings from their rate or exclusion.

features.name: Invoicing and accounts receivable
features.description: An Invoicing module tracking invoices and AR with completed, pending, and cancelled sections, a last-invoiced column, total AR that excludes archived and deposit-in-progress jobs, and a per-invoice Communication history listing every invoice email and text with time, recipient, subject, delivery status, and sender. Supports deposit waivers, recording payments as deposits, and downloadable invoice PDFs. Prompt 38: the Email invoice / Text invoice buttons merged into one split Send control (primary = email + text with the compose modal and text confirm both shown before anything sends; caret = one channel; missing channels send what is on file with a skipped note). Same send code underneath: kind='invoice' SMS with the pay link + STOP line, the compose modal, and the invoice_first_sent_at first-send stamp on either channel. Prompt 40: manual completion is the source of truth. Completed AR rows that were AUTO-completed (jobs.status_manual_at null) but still have a schedule day after today are parked in a 'Completed, but still on the schedule' section and excluded from Total AR; a 'Ready to invoice' section lists in_progress jobs whose last scheduled day has passed, each with a Mark Complete button (markJobComplete, which now also stamps status_manual_at). Schedule spans reach AR rows via the dripjobs_deal_id bridge with the normalized name+address fallback, all reads batched.
