Prompt 45: the job invoice gains a Payment schedule card (Due-now stat, schedule editor, Prepare deposit), and the send flow is extracted into pecInvoiceSendKit so the Approvals view sends held installments through the identical path. Prompt 57: renderJobInvoice reads pec_stripe_pending alongside its other batched fetches and shows in-flight ACH transfers in three places: a muted 'bank transfer clearing' sub-line under Due now (the ask is deliberately NOT reduced; an ACH can bounce), a 'Bank transfer clearing' chip on the covered installment, and a muted pending row above recorded payments with start date and a 3-to-5-business-day expected-by note. Failed transfers render red with the failure message and clear on the AR list's later-payment rule. Prompt 81: the compose modal resolves {{cta}} to empty inside the editor and appends the real View Invoice & Pay button (emailCtaButtonHtml, brand accent, centered) after the editor content at send time, because Quill was stripping the button styling. 2026-08-10: invoice numbers are now digits only. jobs.hq_invoice_number defaults to nextval('pec_invoice_number_seq')::text (series starts 10001, distinct from the 102xxx estimate numbers) and the six native jobs whose display fell back to a lettered uuid slice were backfilled oldest-first; jobs already showing their numeric DripJobs deal id keep it (the number the customer already saw). Invoice terms (2026-08-17): every job carries invoice_terms (due upon completion / due upon receipt / Net 15 / Net 30 / custom date) plus invoice_due_date; defaults come from the client type at accept (commercial = Net 30, residential = due upon completion, settings-tunable), the internal header shows the terms line with an Edit terms modal, net due dates stamp at first send, completion stamps due-upon-completion dates, and the PDF header states the terms. Shared logic: netlify/functions/_pec-invoice-terms.cjs + the pecInvoiceTerms* client mirror. DripJobs-shape invoice page (2026-08-10 rework): the invoice detail is a toolbar (Send invoice, Receive payment, More actions dropdown with PDF / Customer view / Copy link / Charge card / Edit line items / Change order / Record deposit / Mark Complete / Void invoice), one info card (client, invoice number and status, date invoiced, Due on with an inline add, Terms with the editor, salesperson), the money stats, then pill tabs Invoice (line items, change orders, payments) | Settings (payment schedule, deposit flags, void) | Notes (communication history, job-notes pointer). All tab bodies render from the one batched fetch and toggle hidden; state.invoiceTab survives the charge-card refocus re-render. Void invoice is new: jobs.voided_at with the reason in the activity log; pec_job_ar filters voided rows so AR and the pay link self-heal. Cross-nav (2026-08-10): the invoice toolbar shows Open estimate next to Open job card (source estimate resolved by an 8th batched query in renderJobInvoice; hidden when the job has no estimate).

features.name: Deposits and payment schedules
features.description: Partial invoicing on the one-invoice-per-job model (prompt 45). Accepting an estimate prepares an unsent deposit installment at the resolved default (per-job deposit amount, else the system type's deposit_pct, else the settings default_deposit_pct); staff send it manually. Each invoice can carry a schedule of installments, entered as dollars or a percent of the total (both stored, dollars snapshotted), due on job milestones (acceptance / job start / completion; manual and date exist in schema). Exactly one installment is ever the current ask; the shared resolver in _pec-installments.cjs is the single definition used by the pay page, Stripe, the reminder drip, and the staff UI (client mirror pecInstallmentAsk). Milestone-fired installments queue into an approval hold on the drip runner tick (auto-send via Quo/Resend when the gate is off and the master switch is on); approving sends through the normal invoice send kit with a paid/voided/out-of-turn re-check. The pay page shows the current amount due plus the whole plan, kind=installment charges exactly the server-computed current ask, the webhook settles covered installments, and reminders reference the current ask. A job with no installments behaves exactly as before. Prompt 74: the schedule can now be created ON THE ESTIMATE before the customer signs (estimate_installments, mirroring this table minus computed_amount; dollars compute at render and freeze at signature). The estimator's Payment schedule card seeds a deposit + balance pair from the shared resolveDepositPct (system deposit_pct, else default_deposit_pct, else 50), validates that rows resolve to the total exactly, and the customer page recomputes percent rows live as options are ticked (cents allocation, last row absorbs, decline clamp). On accept the frozen signature schedule is copied here as planned rows, REPLACING the auto-prepared deposit (skip-if-any-rows idempotency; jobs.deposit_amount mirrored). estimate_schedule_enabled turns the estimate-side card off company-wide. Auto-seed (2026-08-18): every NEW estimate starts pre-filled with the default schedule (deposit percent from the dominant system type, else default_deposit_pct; remaining balance due at completion) so the customer proposal always shows a payment plan; the first hand edit or Remove schedule ends auto behavior for the session, edits of existing estimates never auto-seed, and the estimate_schedule_autoseed setting (missing = ON) turns it off company-wide from Settings > Invoicing.

features.name: Metrics and analytics
features.description: A Metrics dashboard of DripJobs-style KPI cards where every metric is drillable to the jobs behind it, filtered by time window and salesperson. Prompt 50: the window control is four presets (MTD default via the metrics_default_window setting, YTD, Last 4 weeks = rolling 28 days, Custom with native date inputs); metricsWindowRange/metricsBuildBuckets drive the WHOLE tab (KPIs, deltas vs an equal-length prior period, charts, Sales section, drip/blast cards, drills), routing around invBuildWeeks; the 12-week preset folded into Custom. A manual-generate AI insights panel at the top writes a plain-language read of the computed values for the selected window (pec-metrics-ai.cjs mode:'tab', cache keyed by window+salesperson in the metrics_tab_ai_insights settings row, TTL from metrics_ai_cache_days), distinct from the weekly pipeline read which stays. Main weekly charts render as Chart.js (lazy CDN, pinned, CSS-bar fallback) with theme-aware ink; speed-to-lead and price-per-sqft draw as gradient-area trend lines, conversion by source gets a rate bar chart, and the Sales volume / Revenue collected / Jobs completed cards carry SVG sparklines. Includes AR-timing KPIs and a Sales section: price per square foot by month and system, speed to lead, conversion by source and campaign, an Outbound touches card, the open pipeline with the AI weekly read, and the Phase 3 drip/blast performance cards. Prompt 66: the three by-crew cards derive the crew lead from pec_prod_jobs.crew_id -> pec_prod_crews.name via one shared crewLeadOf helper (pec_prod_jobs.crew_lead is a dead column, never written); the callback rate counts touch-ups (is_callback, incl. $0 warranty revisits) OR the legacy callback flag, charged to the ORIGINAL job's crew via original_job_id, with all touch-up rows excluded from the completed-jobs denominator; and the tab gets All/Sales/Production/Admin category tabs, a pure display filter (data-metcat tags + data-metcat-active on the wrapper, state.metricsCategory) that never re-runs the queries, keeps the AI insights panel reading the whole window, and resizes Chart.js charts on reveal via Chart.getChart over the view's canvases.

features.name: Change orders
features.description: Staff add a change order to a job with a system and square footage so pricing suggests itself like the estimator (or a simple title-and-amount mode), and materials and labor flow into job costing. An Additional coat mode adds an extra coat (MVB today, extensible ADDITIONAL_COATS list) to a chosen existing area at its square footage, with an editable price down to $0 for cost-only absorption; the coat rides the area machinery so its product reaches the material pull and costing automatically. The customer signs online, and when a job has two or more unsigned change orders they can be bundled into one approval link and page where a single signature approves them all, with a live link that picks up any change order added later. Prompt 58: change orders render itemized on the job detail page even when a signature row is missing (line-item boxes marked 'Recorded, no signature link', footer total tied to the line items / coSum), and the printed work order gets a CHANGE ORDERS section on page 1 near the scope with name, detail, sqft/system for scope-mode COs, and price. Prompt 72: openChangeOrderModal accepts a prefill (the declined-line add-back opens AREA mode prefilled from the declined estimate area at the ORIGINALLY quoted price with a quoted-on note; the auto-pricer never overwrites it, and the declined area's product picks ride onto the CO row while the system still matches; a declined CUSTOM line prefills Simple mode). Prompt 81: both approval emails (single and batch) build their Review & sign button with emailCtaButtonHtml (accent from pec_brand_identity instead of a hardcoded hex, centered) and the raw-URL fallback line under the button is gone.

features.name: Subcontractor expenses
features.description: An itemized subcontractor card on job costing records who was paid what on subbed-out work, flowing into the job's costs and profit. A whole job can be flagged as subcontracted so hours expectations and crew bonus math skip it.

features.name: Personal to-dos
features.description: A private per-user checklist in the left menu where each person adds items, checks them off, and deletes them. Lists are completely private (not even admins can see them) and sync across every device the user signs in from.

features.name: Admin Ops Queue
features.description: Admin-only Ops Queue view (Overview nav group): one screen of everything stalled or incomplete, so the admin side runs without being told where to look. Ten DERIVED checks computed at render time from live data (unmapped BusyBusy names; costings submitted-not-finalized, read from pec_prod_jobs.costing_submitted_at/costing_finalized_at; scheduled/in-progress/completed jobs with no revenue, callbacks exempt; completed jobs never invoiced; jobs with no salesperson; jobs with no system via the prompt-55 shared estimate helper; drips held for approval; touch-ups open past a threshold; deposits uncollected past a threshold; system health = the schema-drift probe plus open pec_sync_stuck_reports), each row deep-linking to the screen that fixes it, each check toggleable with day thresholds in Settings > General under Ops Queue. Manual items (title, note, assignee from admin_users, due date, Done) and per-record dismissals of derived rows live in pec_ops_items, the only storage; a dismissal is an 'auto' row keyed by check_key (partial unique) so one job's dismissal never hides another's, and derived rows have no Done, they disappear when the data is fixed. Nav badge = open manual items, ONE head-count query at boot (derived checks are page-load work on the view only). Bell: pec_ops_item_notify (SECURITY DEFINER RPC) writes one pec_notifications row (type ops_item, target_view ops) for NEW MANUAL items only; derived checks never bell. RLS staff-read/admin-write via existing is_admin_staff/is_admin_role; no permission changes. NOT the prompt-49 follow-up queue (sales-side, in Leads). The CRM job detail has an admin '+ Ops Queue' action that prefills the item's deep link.

features.name: Notifications
features.description: A live notification bell in the top bar for events like costing submitted or sent back, payments edited or deleted, customer portal activity, and customer estimate views. Notifications are clickable and route straight to their source (the job's costing view, the invoice, the job card, or the estimate card), respecting each user's access. Prompt 75: rows can target a single user (pec_notifications.target_user_id; NULL means shared, exactly as every pre-75 row). The bell loads shared rows plus your own targeted rows; this is a display filter, not a security boundary (staff RLS still reads the whole table), and read_at stays one shared column. First targeted use: the estimate_viewed_rep personal bell for the salesperson on a viewed estimate. Prompt 78: estimate-view rows are written name-first with the view ordinal (renderBellPanel prints n.body verbatim, so this is a write-time change in logEstimateView only; no renderer change, no backfill).

features.name: People directory and birthdays
features.description: One person = one record (prompt 54). public.people is the source of truth for a person's IDENTITY (name, preferred name, email, phone, month/day birthday, active) across the three legacy person tables: admin_users (logins), pec_sales_team_members (sales reps), pec_prod_crew_members (crew). Roles are the three nullable pointer columns on people; a role is held iff its pointer is set, so the role flag and the identity map can never disagree. Wage, commission %, exclude_from_commission, and crew assignment deliberately STAY on the legacy tables with their readers; Settings > People edits them there inline. Server-side triggers mirror both ways: people edits write through to the legacy rows (name/active, changed fields only), and legacy inserts/renames (pec-create-staff, the legacy cards) auto-adopt/follow so the old surfaces cannot diverge the model. The mirror is switch-off-able via the people_mirror_enabled setting (real rollback, no deploy). Renames are commission-safe: pec_sales_team_members.name_aliases captures every former name via a trigger on that table, and renderCommission resolves aliases (see Commission tracking). Dedupe across the old tables is HUMAN-CONFIRMED only: auto-merge happened solely on matching auth_user_id in the migration backfill; everything else is a suggestion on the Possible duplicates card with Merge (pec_people_merge RPC) / Keep separate (dismissals in the people_merge_dismissed setting). Birthdays: month/day only, NO year stored and no age shown anywhere, required on new adds, backfill nag (dashboard banner + People tab list) until every active person has one, and a reminder at birthday_reminder_lead_days (default 7) as an admin dashboard banner plus a global bell (daily scheduled pec-birthday-reminders.cjs, type 'birthday', target_view 'people' deep-links admins to Settings > People). In-app only; nothing is emailed or texted. Prompt 57 Part H: Settings > Users merged INTO People. One People tab (the 'users' settingsTab key routes there for old deep links); the person modal gains an admin-only Login section with role, the delegable permission checkboxes (PEC_DELEGABLE_PERMS, hoisted to module scope), the Finalize-costing admin checkbox, linked-auth status, Reset password, Delete login (last-admin guarded), and a Create login button for people without one. Create login runs pec-create-staff then folds the adopt-trigger's auto-created person back into the SAME person via the pec_people_merge RPC (the trigger inserts, it does not match by email). The sign-in log lives in a collapsed card at the bottom of the People tab. The old bulk Save-permissions grid is replaced by per-person save inside the modal.

features.name: Per-user permissions
features.description: Role and per-view access controls managed in Settings, defaulting all-on with an admin super-role, so each staff account only sees the views it should (Job Costing, Bonus Report, Commission, Catalog, and Settings are admin-only). Staff accounts, roles, and access are added and managed in the Settings Users area. Prompt 54: staff identity now also lives on public.people (one record per person across logins, sales, crew); admin_users remains the auth/RLS record and is mirrored from people by triggers, and a new admin_users row (pec-create-staff) is auto-adopted as a person. Settings > People is the unified surface; Users stays the place for logins, roles, permissions, and password resets. Prompt 57: renderSettingsUsers is retired; role and permission management moved into the person modal's Login section on Settings > People (see 'People directory and birthdays'). Permission semantics are unchanged: missing row = all capabilities, admins are full-access with Finalize costing as the one restrictable capability, saves keep the pre-migration can_finalize_costing retry.

features.name: Grouped navigation rail
features.description: The left menu is organized into flyout groups (Overview, Sales, Sales Pipeline, Estimates, Drips, Production, Finance, Settings, and a pinned Help) that open a submenu of screens, replacing the long flat list, with a mobile Menu button. The Sales Pipeline group's Pipeline item opens the lead board (the page header reads Sales Pipeline via the button's data-pec-title; the view key and #leads bookmarks are unchanged, and Production's Jobs pipeline is a different screen). Jobs pipeline lives under Production; Settings, Pricing, and Sync Health under Settings; the Drips and Settings groups hide entirely for non-admins. Old bookmarks and links keep working. Prompt 65 (Part D): the Sales Pipeline group was renamed Sales Activity and its Pipeline button renamed Sales Pipeline (data-pec-view="leads" and data-pec-title unchanged; Production's Jobs pipeline untouched).

features.name: What's New changelog
features.description: A plain-language changelog that surfaces new features in a sign-in popup once, keeps the full history in a Help card, and grounds the help assistant. Each user-facing change ships with an entry describing what it does and how to use it.

features.name: In-app help assistant
features.description: A bottom-right Help chat bubble that answers how-to and where-is questions about the app, grounded in a CRM help document, the SOPs, and the What's New history. It explains features and orients users without performing actions or changing data.

features.name: SOP hub
features.description: A standard-operating-procedure hub with an AI SOP chat backend for company processes and documentation. It is kept out of the owner-facing front end but remains available in the codebase.

features.name: Cockpit and JARVIS
features.description: A separate Cockpit workspace reached from the sidebar's Daily flow card, with Dashboard, Execution, and JARVIS tabs. JARVIS is an AI strategy assistant, and the Dashboard gives a quick read on the current state of the business including booked sales.

features.name: Claude-facing MCP server
features.description: A Model Context Protocol server exposing read-only tools (sales summary, customers, jobs, schedule, pipeline) so Claude can answer questions about the business directly against live data. Sixth tool get_sales_recordings (2026-07-28): read-only list of SalesAsk sales visit recordings from pec_salesask_recordings (AI summary, action items, process score, recording link; filters customer/rep/date window; transcripts excluded to keep payloads small).

features.name: Customer portal
features.description: A customer-facing portal, styled to the TopCoat brand, where the customer picks their flake color and signs off, sees an editable per-status project description, and views per-area budget details. Portal activity raises notifications on the internal side.

features.name: Hosted invoice and pay page
features.description: A public, branded invoice page at a private /pay/<token> link where customers view line items and pay online. Redesigned to a premium look with the amount due front and center, it hides pay buttons and shows a PENDING state while a bank transfer clears so no one pays twice. With a payment schedule (prompt 45) the page shows the current amount due as the hero, the full installment plan with paid/upcoming states, and project total/paid/remaining; without one it renders exactly the legacy full-balance page. Invoice terms (2026-08-17): the hero and the bill-to band state the terms and due date at the top (mirroring DripJobs); informational only, the schedule/ask still owns every amount and the due box, and a paid invoice shows the terms label with no date.

features.name: Stripe card and ACH payments
features.description: Online payments through Stripe: customers pay invoices by card or bank transfer (ACH) from the pay link, an internal Charge card option runs a hosted payment for office staff, and payments attach to a named Stripe Customer. ACH settles asynchronously over 3-5 days, recording itself on clearing, showing pending markers, and raising a failure alert and red chip if a transfer bounces. Includes editable and deletable (audited, cascade-guarded) payment records with an activity log. kind=installment (prompt 45) charges exactly the current installment amount computed server-side from the token; the webhook settles covered installments after recording. Prompt 57: pending markers now also appear on the JOB INVOICE page (Due now sub-line, schedule chip, Payments row), not just the AR list; the browser still never writes pec_stripe_pending and no pec_payments row exists until the webhook settles the transfer.

features.name: Resend email pipeline
features.description: A transactional email pipeline (Resend) for sending branded invoices and documents with a compose-before-send step, a Settings Email panel, editable templates with a real-view preview, and per-send delivery logging.

features.name: Email log
features.description: A top-level Email Log view (all staff, like Messages) listing every email the system sent from pec_email_log, newest first, with a customer name/address search, type and status filters, a date range, and delivery detail (opens, clicks, bounces from the Resend webhook). Clicking a row opens the full email: transactional sends store their final wrapped HTML in pec_email_log.body_html going forward (rendered in a sandboxed iframe), drip and blast rows read their body from the pec_drip_sends ledger (provider_id = resend_id), and rows that predate body capture show a clear not-captured note. The same rows embed read-only as an Emails card at the bottom of the customer detail and job detail pages. PEC only, no brand filter. Known gaps: internal office alert emails (invoice payment-intent, estimate accept/decline, Stripe ACH-failure) and Supabase auth emails (password resets) do not write pec_email_log.

features.name: Quo / OpenPhone integration
features.description: Integration with the office phone (Quo/OpenPhone) powering two-way SMS from customer profiles and jobs, a Text invoice button that sends the pay link, STOP-based opt-out enforcement, and automatic call logging with AI summaries, next steps, and full transcripts on customer profiles and lead timelines.

features.name: DripJobs integration
features.description: The inbound-deal integration that auto-bridges DripJobs proposals into the CRM via webhooks (proposal accepted, stage changed, project completed), writing jobs to both the Jobs page and the Job Schedule. A DripJobs Sync Health view makes missing, partial, or silently failed ingestion visible so staff can confirm jobs are syncing.

features.name: CompanyCam integration
features.description: Job photos come from CompanyCam via a staff-authenticated proxy, with a searchable project picker on the job detail and a navigable fullscreen photo viewer that zooms and pans (double click, wheel, pinch). The Job Schedule's +Schedule modal shows the same photos read-only.

features.name: BusyBusy hours import (Payroll Export)
features.description: Crew hours reach job costing through an admin-triggered, preview-then-commit import from the BusyBusy Payroll Export API (Settings > BusyBusy). The API is a snapshot, not a sync (calculated Ids, no updatedSince, no deletion feed), so each import atomically replaces the stored date window via the pec_busybusy_import RPC; re-importing after punch corrections is the normal workflow. Identity is name-only (the export's EmployeeId is empty): every exported name is mapped to a crew member or Ignored on the mapping screen, and projects link to jobs once by exact normalized customer name, then by their stable 7-digit ProjectNumber (no fuzzy matching, ever). Overtime is BusyBusy's weekly-40 attribution, stored verbatim as REG/OT1 rows (a punch crossing hour 40 arrives as a split pair sharing Start/End); hours aggregate at read time, and BusyBusy's Wage/Cost columns are deliberately never imported. Overhead projects (Shop) are stored and reported but never charge a job. Anomalies (long punches, overlaps, punch notes) import and are flagged in the preview, never auto-corrected. Manual labor entry remains for jobs with no BusyBusy coverage; a job with imported rows uses them and shows its manual entries greyed. The earlier GraphQL proxy (pec-busybusy.cjs, 401 since 2026-06-13, spec docs/archive/prompts/claude-code-prompt-busybusy-overtime-costing.md) was retired by this build. Prompt 54: crew-member identity (pec_prod_crew_members.id, which pec_prod_busybusy_employees.crew_member_id maps to) is untouched by the People model; the mirror only writes name/active and never rewrites ids, so imported-hour attribution is stable. Prompt 56: imported hours now reach gross profit, not just the Bonus Payout box. bbAccumulateEntries is the one accumulation rule, loadCostingData builds the shared per-job map, and crewLaborForJob turns it into the loaded labor cost that computeCostingRow charges against GP on the costing card, the Rollups, and Metrics. Prompt 57: punch times display 12-hour with am/pm in the import preview and in the server-built anomaly detail strings (fmtPunch in pec-busybusy-export.cjs); pure string reformats of the Arizona-local azTimestamp values, with stored rows, dedupe keys, and comparisons untouched. Prompt 68: the WRITE side (project auto-creation on estimate acceptance) is its own entry, 'BusyBusy project auto-creation (Zapier hook)'; because the accept path pre-writes the pec_prod_busybusy_projects row with the estimate digits as project_number, this importer's number-first match resolves auto-created projects with no human mapping step.

features.name: BusyBusy project auto-creation (Zapier hook)
features.description: When a customer accepts an estimate, the accept path (ensureJobCreated in pec-public-estimate.cjs) fires a fire-and-forget POST at a Zapier Catch Hook (env ZAPIER_BUSYBUSY_HOOK_URL, shared secret ZAPIER_BUSYBUSY_HOOK_SECRET in both an x-topcoat-secret header and a body field) whose Zap runs BusyBusy Create Project, so the crew's clock-in project exists without anyone hand-creating it. Architecture is forced: Zapier MCP tools are assistant-side (a Netlify function cannot call them), export.busybusy.io is read-only, and graphql.busybusy.io has 401'd since 2026-06-13, so the Catch Hook is the only outbound path (the Routemize intake pattern in reverse). Naming (Dylan, prompt 68): title = customer name exactly as stored, project_number = the estimate number's digits, customer = the customer name; the title deliberately carries NO estimate number so the importer's normalized name match stays viable as a fallback, and the number is supplied so the NAME-ONCE-THEN-NUMBER link never has to be discovered: the accept path pre-writes the pec_prod_busybusy_projects row (project_number, project_name, job_id; linked_by/linked_at NULL = pending, the table's existing nullable convention) BEFORE the POST, so the link exists even when the Zap run is slow or fails, and the unique partial indexes make a concurrent double-accept lose the insert race and skip the POST. Contract: the acceptance can NEVER fail because BusyBusy did (maybeCreateBusybusyProject in _pec-busybusy.cjs never throws, 4s abort on the fetch, and the call site adds its own try/catch); no env var = clean no-op; idempotent via an existing-row check on job_id OR project_number; callback/touch-up jobs never create a project; reminders off and onsite_verification 'none' on creation with the geofence radius stored so verification can be enabled later. Settings > BusyBusy > Project auto-create (rule 12): on/off (busybusy_autocreate_enabled), geofence radius meters min 100 (busybusy_autocreate_radius_m, default 150), reminders (busybusy_autocreate_reminders). The printed work order's Job Identity grid replaced the dead DJ # pair with Clock in # (renderWorkOrder resolves pec_prod_busybusy_projects.project_number via the deal-id bridge or estimates.pec_prod_job_id; a job with no number falls back to the DripJobs id when one exists, Dylan-approved, else prints blank; same single pair, so the prompt-53 header height math is untouched). Fixture suite production/busybusy-project.test.cjs drives the real modules including ensureJobCreated surviving a rejected fetch and a hook 500. The Zap itself is built in the Zapier web UI (Cowork handoff, PROJECT-LOG 2026-08-04).

features.name: Google Sheets bridge
features.description: The original data bridge using Google Sheets (Booked Jobs and Dashboard Data sheets) via an Apps Script proxy to feed the dashboard's booked-sales and revenue figures, since migrated toward Supabase-native reads.

features.name: Slack notifications
features.description: Outbound Slack alerts to the #epoxysales channel for key sales and production events: estimate accepted or declined, costings sent back with their reason, and (prompt 75) every customer open of a sent estimate with the price, salesperson, which open it is, and time since sent (switchable via estimate_view_slack_enabled in Settings > Estimates).

features.name: Revenue goals home
features.description: Owner home screen tracking booked-sales revenue pace plus the annual scorecard, rocks, meeting rhythm, and projects cards, sourced from Google Sheets.

features.name: Owner task list
features.description: Owner personal task list synced through a Google Sheet, separate from crew tasks and the private per-user to-dos.

features.name: Staff authentication
features.description: Supabase email and password sign-in with owner-versus-employee shell gating, password reset, a global auth gate, and sign-in event logging.

features.name: Job activity log
features.description: Per-job audit trail card showing who changed what and when, plus the job status-change modal.

features.name: Admin landing dashboard
features.description: The admin CRM landing view shown after sign-in, giving a quick overview before drilling into specific screens.

features.name: Color catalog admin
features.description: Admin screen for the flake color catalog: add and edit colors that feed the customer portal color picker and material ordering.

features.name: Referrals tracking
features.description: Simple tracking of customer referrals with an add/edit form.

features.name: Reviews
features.description: The working surface for Google review attribution (prompt 60). Lists EVERY review 1-5 stars (stars, reviewer, text, source, matched job + crew leader) with a match-status badge that keeps inference visually distinct from fact: Unmatched / Auto-matched (amber, machine guess) / Confirmed (green, human) / Rejected. Per row: Confirm match (auto -> confirmed; on a qualifying rating this is the ONLY thing that creates a pec_review_bonuses row), Reassign to a different job (searchable picker; a human pick lands as confirmed, crew snapshot from that job's ask), and Reject (clears linkage, reopens the claimed ask). A second tab, 'Asked, no review yet', lists open asks with days-since-ask, phone and email: a FILTER for Anne, deliberately not a queue (no notifications, no Ops count, no bell; decision 14). Bad-review bells (pec-review-intake) click through to this view.

features.name: Review request drip
features.description: NiceJob-style Google review campaign (prompt 60). Marking a job complete (any of the four completion paths) pops 'Send a Google review request?' with Send preselected (review_ask_default_on); BOTH branches write a pec_review_requests row (a recorded skip is distinguishable from forgetting), Send snapshots crew_lead/crew_id from pec_prod_jobs at ask time (frozen; schedule edits never rewrite attribution) and enrolls the 'review' drip kind: 4 touches, day 1 SMS / 3 SMS / 7 email / 14 SMS, copy naming the crew leader when one is on the snapshot and generic wording when not, the /r/<token> tracking link appended by CODE (pec-review-redirect logs the click first-write-wins and ALWAYS 302s to google_review_link_epoxy, even on total failure). Stops on: review detected, customer reply, touch-up/callback opened (review_stop_on_touchup), job closed, STOP/opt-out, and bad_review (a review at or below review_alert_max_stars raises a pec_notifications bell for Dylan and Anne and stops the drip). Google-policy rails: no incentives ever (system prompt + mechanical reviewCopyViolation scrub) and no rating-gating anywhere; the close-out popup is an internal choice about whom to ask, never a customer-facing happiness screen. SHIPPED mode='live' behind the approval gate (decision 15, unlike the other three kinds): an enroll-time guard refuses to enroll while drip_approval_required is not 'true' and the campaign has never had an approved send. Reviews arrive via pec-review-intake.cjs (Zapier Google Business Profile webhook, REVIEW_INTAKE_SECRET header): idempotent on external_id, auto-matches at most match_status='auto' (name similarity + crew-leader mention + click evidence, ties stay unmatched), NEVER writes 'confirmed'. Confirmed reviews at or above review_bonus_min_stars pay a flat review_bonus_amount to the crew leader via pec_review_bonuses, a ledger deliberately separate from job costing (never touches pec_prod_job_bonuses or bonus_cost/GP; decision 13). Metrics > Reviews shows the ask funnel and the per-crew-leader confirmed-count scoreboard; Settings > Reviews holds the seven review_* keys; scripts/backfill-review-asks.cjs enrolls the last 30 days of completions anchored to enrollment time (one due step, never three).

features.name: Schedule status auto-sync
features.description: Boot-time sweep plus a scheduled daily function that flip job status from scheduled to in progress based on the production schedule, so statuses stay honest without manual edits. The one canonical rule is deriveJobStatus (client) in lockstep with the pec_prod_jobs_sync_public_status trigger (2026-07-21_manual_completion_source_of_truth.sql). Since 2026-07-21 nothing auto-completes: a job past its last scheduled day stays in_progress until a human marks it complete, and only the manual completion paths stamp completed_date.

features.name: Appointments calendar
features.description: A top-level Appointments view (Sales group, all staff): a Month/Week/Day calendar of sales appointments (on-site estimates, project walkthroughs, site visits, and ad-hoc 'other' blocks), separate from the crew Job Schedule. Each appointment is assigned to a pec_sales_team_members roster member (per-member event color, per-type accent, type + salesperson filters with an All Users default). Create from the New Appointment button or a day/slot tap; edit, cancel, delete, drag-to-reschedule and resize. Renders with FullCalendar 6 lazy-loaded from cdnjs and degrades to a month list that still edits when the CDN is blocked. Booking a lead-linked appointment notifies the bell (log_appointment_booked RPC) and kicks pec-appt-notify for the consent-checked customer confirmation; the scheduled pec-appt-reminder-runner sends the configured offset reminders (rules edited in Settings > Appointments). Schedule Estimate on a lead prefills the form and, on booking an on-site estimate, advances a new or contacted lead to the Estimate Scheduled pipeline stage (a NEW lead also stamps contacted_at); canceling or deleting the lead's last scheduled on-site estimate walks the lead back to Contacted (apptCancelLeadEffects, client and server twins), while a reschedule that leaves another scheduled visit keeps the stage. Prompt 38: appointment notes are split into customer-facing Job notes (pec_appointments.customer_notes, appended to the customer's confirmation/reminder texts and emails on both channels, scrubbed of em dashes) and internal Company notes (pec_appointments.notes, pushed to the Google event description composed with an auto-added customer name/phone + a /?appt=<id> TopCoat deep link above a '----' separator; the pull ingests only the human-typed part back). The appointment popup also shows the linked lead/customer's phone with tap-to-call and tap-to-text. Prompt 43: booking a lead-linked appointment also pauses the lead's active nurture drip (enrollment stopped with reason appointment_booked) via the shared server helper apptBookingLeadEffects in _pec-appt.cjs, called from the pec-appt-notify on-book kick; appointments can also arrive from Routemize (see the Routemize appointment intake entry). Prompt 65 (Part C): the edit modal's footer has a Start estimate button (edit mode only, never on an unsaved appointment, and deliberately NOT on the calendar chip: month chips are ~20px with drag-to-reschedule live). It closes the modal and creates a draft estimate from the SAVED row: lead-linked through createDraftEstimate (duplicate guard before the insert), customer-only through createDraftEstimateNow, both -> lead path, neither -> the New Estimate modal on New Contact prefilled from the appointment so the customer row is created first. The appointment's location_* address and customer_notes carry onto the estimate (address wins over customer billing; notes to crew_notes). Prompt 67: custom Google Calendar-shape chips via eventContent (apptChipContent). Month view renders tinted pills (appointment-type dot, short start time like '9am', customer name ellipsised; background = member color at 14% over the card token, ink text, member-color left bar); week/day render solid blocks (member color deepened 22% toward ink so white text clears 4:1 on every palette entry) stacking name, type label, and city/short address, collapsing lines by DURATION (under 60 min drops the place line, under 30 min collapses to one line; classes set in apptEventFromRow, no resize observer). All-day events keep the solid treatment with no time in every view. The chip's 'who' comes from apptDisplayName: customers(name) rides the range query as a PostgREST embed (real FK; on an embed error the query retries plain so the calendar never blanks), lead names come from ONE batched leads .in() read merged as row._lead because pec_appointments.lead_id deliberately has no FK (survives lead soft-delete) so an embed is impossible; precedence customer -> lead business/full/first+last -> title name half (apptTitleNameHalf, shared with the prompt-65 Start-estimate split) -> type label. Event objects no longer set backgroundColor/borderColor (CSS custom properties --pec-member/--pec-type own the visuals); drag, resize, and eventClick all still ride the FullCalendar harness (chips are plain divs/spans, pointer events bubble). The legend's meaning is unchanged: round dot = salesperson, square dot = type, both still true of the chips. The CRM has no dark theme today (pecCurrentTheme hardcodes light); chip tints mix against theme tokens so a future dark theme flows through without chip rework.

features.name: Routemize appointment intake
features.description: The webhook path that makes Routemize (prescottepoxycompany.routemize.com) the booking front end and TopCoat's appointment calendar the system of record. Routemize's NATIVE Custom Webhook ('TopCoat appointment intake') posts all five appointment events (Created / Updated / StatusChanged / Cancelled / Deleted) directly to pec-appt-intake with the shared x-webhook-secret header; there is NO Zapier in the chain (prompt 56 replaced the prompt-43 Zapier design). The endpoint auto-detects the body shape: a Routemize envelope ({eventType, data}) is mapped by mapRoutemizeEnvelope onto the original hand-rolled contract, which still works for manual curls. eventType casing is normalized aggressively (PascalCase, dotted lowercase); unrecognized events return 200 no-op, never 4xx, because Routemize retries non-2xx and tracks webhook health. Mapping: relatedEntityId -> routemize_appt_id (upsert key), startTime/endTime carry explicit Z (trusted as-is, no Phoenix branch), contactName/contact.* -> customer fields, address.* -> location_*, customerAnswers -> customer-facing Q&A in customer_notes, nested AppointmentNotes -> internal notes, appointmentTitle ignored in favor of our own '<name>, <service>' title. appt_type comes from the routemize_service_type_map settings key (serviceName then eventTypeId, lowercased; unmapped defaults to on_site_estimate), editable in Settings > Appointments > Routemize booking intake (rule 12). Rep mapping tries assignedUsers[0].userName then .email against pec_sales_team_members.google_email, then first+last name, case-insensitive. Lead behavior (native path only, REVERSES prompt 43 decision 3): an unmatched booker gets a lead CREATED (brand PEC, stage new, sms_consent false, source = Routemize's own leadSourceText/leadSource slug else 'routemize', source_ref + routemize_contact_id = contact.contactId), then apptBookingLeadEffects advances it like an in-app booking; the created lead is deliberately NOT nurture-enrolled (the effects would pause it instantly). Matching uses the shared same-human rule in _pec-lead-match.cjs (also used by pec-lead-intake, windowless here), so the two intakes cannot drift; a matched existing lead gets its source filled only if blank (never overwritten), contact.contactId stored fill-if-blank (column absence tolerated pre-migration), and a 'note' lead_event recording the booking; a matched customer stores the contactId and suppresses lead creation. AppointmentStatusChanged is read defensively (shape unverified): a cancel-ish status cancels, anything else (including no readable status) is treated as an update with the ambiguity noted in internal notes, never a cancellation. A Routemize cancel/delete marks the row canceled, never hard-deletes, so the existing Google push removes the calendar event on its next kick. google_* columns are never touched. Every attempt logs the RAW envelope to pec_webhook_ingest_log (endpoint 'appt-intake') for the Sync Health view. Prompt 65 (Part A): Routemize sends question UUIDs in customerAnswers[].question, and customer_notes rides on every customer confirmation/reminder (both channels), so ID-shaped question keys (UUID, or a 16+ char space-free opaque token containing a digit) are stripped at intake by mapCustomerAnswers/isIdLikeQuestionKey (exported, unit-tested in production/appt-notes.test.cjs); the line keeps just the answer, real question text keeps the 'Question: answer' shape. Prompt 73 Part A: customerAnswers are now ROUTED by questionId via the routemize_answer_routing settings JSON (Settings > Appointments > Routemize booking questions): 'customer' answers build customer_notes (UUID-shaped question keys still stripped), 'internal' answers land on the rep-only notes as 'Service requested: <answer>', 'drop' discards, and an unmapped questionId defaults to customer. Live seed routes the free-text project description to customer and the service picker to internal, so reminders stop ending with a dangling picker value. Cancellations also re-enroll an eligible lead into nurture from step 1 (see Lead drip engine).

features.name: Google Calendar two-way sync
features.description: Per-member Google Calendar sync for the Appointments calendar. Each roster member connects their OWN Google account from Settings > Appointments (OAuth: pec-google-oauth-start mints an HMAC-signed-state consent URL, pec-google-oauth-callback exchanges the code, creates-or-reuses a dedicated 'TopCoat' secondary calendar in their account, and stores tokens in the service-role-only pec_sales_member_google_tokens vault; connection status the UI reads lives as flags on pec_sales_team_members). TopCoat pushes appointment create/update/cancel/delete into that TopCoat calendar (pec-appt-sync-push, kicked fire-and-forget from apptPostWrite), and the scheduled pec-google-calendar-pull polls it every 15 minutes with incremental syncTokens (410 = full resync), upserting by google_event_id with an echo/last-writer-wins rule on google_updated. Personal (primary) calendars are never read or written. Requires GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID/SECRET in Netlify env; everything no-ops cleanly while unconfigured. Prompt 38: the pushed event description = internal Company notes + a separator + an auto-added contact/link block (composeGcalDescription/stripGcalDescription in _pec-google.cjs); the pull strips the auto block so a Google-side description edit only ever lands in notes, and customer_notes never crosses to or from Google.

features.name: Address autocomplete (HQ)
features.description: Google Places address autocomplete on the HQ dashboard, ported from the estimator PWA's places.ts onto vanilla index.html (current AutocompleteSuggestion / Place.fetchFields surface, session-token billing hygiene, silent degrade offline or with no key). Wired into the appointment form's address field (fills city/state/zip + location_place_id) and the New Lead modal (which gained split city/state/zip inputs that now persist to the leads columns). Uses the existing domain-restricted browser key from netlify.toml's secret-scan omit list; suggestions only appear once the Maps JavaScript + Places APIs are enabled on that key in Google Cloud Console. Customer/job forms deliberately not wired this pass.

features.name: Migration drift detection
features.description: Detects repo migrations that were never applied to prod (the failure that let 2026-07-18_crew_notes.sql silently break every estimator save for a week). Every migration dated 2026-07-01+ carries a machine-readable @artifacts header (CLAUDE.md rule 13) declaring the tables/columns/indexes/settings it creates; scripts/build-migration-manifest.mjs compiles the headers into netlify/functions/_migration-manifest.json at build time (wired into netlify.toml's build command), and pec-migration-drift.cjs probes every declared artifact against the LIVE schema in one batched pec_schema_probe RPC call (migration 2026-07-25_migration_drift_probe.sql; read-only SECURITY DEFINER, service-role-only). Artifact probing, not filename matching, because schema_migrations names do not match repo filenames, and it also catches PARTIALLY applied migrations. Runs daily at 07:00 MST plus on demand from Settings > Diagnostics > Schema Drift (four buckets: applied / missing / partial / not-verifiable, plus informational reverse drift = live tables no repo SQL creates). Missing/partial raise de-duped admin bells (never re-notifies while one is unread); reverse drift never notifies. Knobs: migration_drift_check_enabled, migration_drift_baseline.

features.name: Estimator stuck-sync visibility
features.description: Replaces the quiet 'N to sync' counter that hid a week of failing saves. Retry policy (production/outbox-drain.cjs, fixture-tested by production/outbox-backoff.test.cjs): per-op backoff 1m/5m/30m then hourly, deliberately NO maximum-attempts cap (the crew_notes incident self-healed only because ops were still retrying); children of a failed or deferred parent are skipped for the pass, transitively, with attempts untouched, so one root cause reads as one problem. Header shows three states: Online, Online · N to sync, or a RED 'N saves not syncing · oldest X days' once any op reaches sync_stuck_threshold_attempts (default 2, reaches the PWA via catalog.ts settings). The red state expands to per-op detail (attempts, stuck-for, lastError verbatim) with a Retry now that force-clears backoff. Server escalation: once per session the PWA POSTs stuck-op metadata (ids and error only) to pec-sync-stuck.cjs, which upserts pec_sync_stuck_reports on op_id and bells the office once per op; gated by sync_stuck_escalation_enabled. Knobs live in Settings > Estimates.

features.name: Two-factor authentication (2FA)
features.description: Opt-in TOTP two-factor authentication for staff logins. A shield button in the topbar (next to logout, visible to every signed-in staff member) opens an enroll/manage modal: scan a QR into an authenticator app, verify a 6-digit code, and 2FA turns on; it can also be turned back off. Enrolled users are challenged for a code at sign-in (passwordSignIn -> pecMfaLoginChallenge); users without a factor pass straight through, so it is inert until someone opts in. Uses the Supabase GoTrue MFA API (no app tables). Enforcement for everyone (gating on AAL2) is a deliberate later step. Requires TOTP enabled in the Supabase Auth dashboard.

features.name: Security hardening & monitoring
features.description: Server-side authorization and monitoring from the 2026-07-25 security review. requireStaff() (in _pec-supabase.cjs) validates a caller's Supabase JWT AND confirms an admin_users row before any service-role endpoint acts (send-sms/email, blast-run, metrics-ai, estimate-*, lead-ai, drip-approve, appt-notify, sheets-proxy, sync-stuck, sop-chat, log-signin, notify-costing-sendback, migration-drift manual). safeEqual() gives constant-time secret compares. DB-side: log_* notification RPCs guard on is_admin_staff and anon EXECUTE revoked; RLS RBAC via has_permission() on commissions/costing/catalog; audit_log made append-only. pec-security-monitor.cjs (scheduled every 15m) Slacks an alert on a staff sign-in from a never-before-seen IP, gated by security_alerts_enabled.

features.name: SalesAsk sales visit recordings
features.description: Integration with SalesAsk (AI recording/coaching for in-home sales). SCHEMA APPLIED TO PROD 2026-08-08 (prompt 77 Part 0; the 2026-07-31 migration had been stranded since it was written, so every surface below rendered its run-the-migration empty state until then). pec-salesask-sync.cjs (cron */15, gated by settings salesask_sync_enabled, still 'false' pending the Cowork env-var handoff) pushes upcoming pec_appointments to SalesAsk's scheduled-tasks API with event_id = appointment id so the rep's mobile recording auto-attaches; it also reconciles recent recordings (SalesAsk webhooks have no retries) and completes pending rows (transcript fetch, appointment matching via event_id -> rep+time-window -> name fuzzy, then a 'salesask_recording' lead_events row that is both the lead-timeline surface and pec-lead-ai's context feed). pec-webhook-salesask.cjs (routed /api/salesask/webhook, ?secret= vs SALESASK_WEBHOOK_SECRET, always-200 after auth) ingests recording.processed thin rows immediately. Recordings land in pec_salesask_recordings (staff-read RLS via is_admin_staff(), which IS this app's any-signed-in-staff predicate, so reps see their own visits; service-role writes; linked to appointment/lead/customer/sales_member). features.name: Customer financing (Enhancify)
features.description: A settings-backed financing block on the public estimate page (between the total and the accept panel), the public invoice page (keyed on balance due, above the pay buttons), and the estimate PDF (static text: monthly estimate plus apply URL). Off by default; nothing renders until financing_enabled is on and the amount clears financing_min_amount. With financing_apr_pct and financing_term_months both set it quotes an estimated monthly payment from the standard amortization formula, always labeled an estimate and subject to credit approval; with either blank it shows a plain check-your-options action. The embed shape is an https iframe URL (financing_embed_url), never a script tag, so a settings row cannot inject script into a customer page; the plain apply link is the degradation path. The customer portal shows a price but is deliberately skipped: settings are staff-only under RLS and the portal is anon via SECURITY DEFINER RPCs, so exposing financing there needs a follow-up migration.

features.name: Global search
features.description: The one topbar search box (#rdSearch, part of the persistent shell so it is on every page) searches jobs, estimates, leads, and customers at once, grouped in that order and capped at 5 per group with a +N more line that opens the type's full list view with its in-list filter set to the query (jobs, which have no in-list text filter, expand in place). Jobs keep the search_jobs RPC (pg_trgm) with a local fallback; estimates match number (102026 or EST-102026), customer name, phone, address; leads match full/business/first/last name, email, phone (archived leads included and badged); customers match name, company, first/last, email, phone. Debounced 250ms with a sequence guard that discards stale result sets wholesale. The in-list search boxes are deliberately kept: they filter a visible table, this box jumps to a record. Clicking a result opens that record's detail page.

features.name: Lost reason AI backfill
features.description: A nightly pass (15:00 UTC) fills lost_reason and lost_notes on already-lost leads that have a matching call and no reason yet, using the same deterministic keyword classifier as the Mark-lost modal's suggestion over the call summary (transcript only when the summary is empty). It can never overwrite a human value (the PATCH re-asserts lost_reason is null) and every fill writes a lost_reason_ai lead_events row the timeline renders as provenance. Gated by the lost_reason_ai_backfill_enabled setting in Settings > Drips (missing row = on).

features.name: On-site presentation view (Present mode)
features.description: SumoQuote-style on-site presentation for closing in the driveway. A Present button on the estimate detail page opens a full-screen, iPad-friendly, dark walkthrough: literature slides (why us + warranty, process, photo gallery + live Google reviews, financing) followed by the estimate itself. The literature comes from pec_presentation_sections, ONE content store with TWO consumers: the same active sections, in the same Settings sort order, also render read-only on the public estimate page below the actions card, so the spouse who was not home re-reads the story from the emailed link. Nothing is stored per estimate; the rep skips or jumps live via the header select, dots, arrow keys, or the Back/Next bar. The estimate slide embeds the EXISTING ?preview= render from pec-public-estimate.cjs via the same staff-JWT srcdoc fetch as the Preview button; there is deliberately NO second line-item or price renderer anywhere (the governing rule: present = the customer view plus literature, never a new estimate). Closing on site: Open for signing runs the shared markEstimateSent flip (confirm-gated when unsent) then loads the REAL public page in the frame as ?token=<public_token>&present=1, so an on-site signature runs the byte-identical accept path as the emailed link (same POST /api/estimate/action, same handleAccept, same job/customer/deposit/webhook effects; proven side-by-side in the 2026-08-02 log entry). present=1's ONLY effect is skipping logEstimateView: the rep is driving, so presenting is not a customer view and must not light the bell mid-pitch. A 5s poll surfaces the signature to the rep chrome (Accepted and signed). Present mode is ONLINE ONLY by decision (no offline caching, no queued signatures). Settings > Presentation (admin): per-brand (PEC/FTP, brand REQUIRED on every row) section editor with create/edit/reorder/activate/delete, markdown body (the mdToSafeHtml subset, customer-facing so no em dashes), and manually curated photos resized client-side to 1600 px JPEG q0.82 before upload to the public pec-presentation bucket (5 MB server backstop); reviews count + minimum star rating are settings keys (presentation_reviews_count, presentation_reviews_min_rating) pulling live from the prompt-60 reviews table. Optional line items render as upgrade CARDS (optcard) on the customer page with the same .opt-toggle inputs and running total, replacing the bare checkbox rows. Tiered good/better/best packages are explicitly out of scope (one price plus optional items). Prompt 78: a hint under Open for signing tells the rep the customer can tick options and sign on the iPad; the blank hard-block rides inside estimateSendGateOk now, so open-for-signing (previously the ONE send channel with no blank check) can no longer bypass it; and after the ticking/interactive flag split the walkthrough's pre-live ?preview= estimate slide is tickable, so the rep can show the price moving before committing to going live.

features.name: Instant lead touch and new-lead alerts
features.description: Prompt 73: the moment an online lead lands (pec-lead-intake webhook), three things happen inline in the same request. (1) The day-0 instant touch: one FIXED thank-you message (no AI), email always, SMS only with consent, bypassing only the approval gate and quiet hours; wording lives on pec_drip_steps step 0 (fixed_template/fixed_subject), tokens {first_name} and {booking_link}. (2) A Slack alert to the leads channel (env SLACK_LEADS_WEBHOOK, falling back to SLACK_OFFICE_WEBHOOK, logged no-op when neither is set) with name, source, tel: phone link, email, project description, instant-touch outcome, and a TopCoat link. (3) A staff bell row (pec_notifications type lead_created, target_view leads) that opens the lead's detail pane. Consent capture: parseSmsConsent accepts the exact Zapier checkbox spellings (true/1/'true'/'yes'/'on'/'1'/'checked'/'agree'/'agreed'/'y'), never arbitrary truthiness; the disclosure text is stored on the created lead_event when the form sends sms_consent_disclosure. Settings > Drips shows the instant-reply toggle (drip_instant_touch_enabled), the Routemize booking link (routemize_booking_url), and a 30-day consent readout so the web-form gap stays visible. ROOT CAUSE NOTE: sms_consent is false on nearly every lead because the WEB FORM does not capture consent; until the form ships a TCPA checkbox mapped into sms_consent, the instant touch and all drips are email-only in practice.

features.name: Deep links and shareable URLs
features.description: The address bar mirrors wherever you are in the CRM as /?v=<view> plus a record id param (job, estimate, lead, customer, invoice), so any screen can be copied from the address bar or pasted into Slack and land a signed-in teammate on the same record. Every record row, pipeline card, global search result, and nav rail flyout item is a real anchor: plain click navigates in-app exactly as before (no reload), ctrl/cmd/middle-click opens a new tab (pecLinkClickGuard). A pasted link opens the outer CRM shell tab first (shared retry-click helper with the legacy ?view=prescott link), consumes once, and permission-gated views land on the dashboard with a toast instead of a blank panel. Back/Forward still walk views, including after arriving from a pasted URL (popstate falls back to parsing the URL). The legacy ?appt=<id> (Google Calendar), ?view=prescott, and ?portal=<token> contracts are untouched. Pipeline kanban drag survives: the anchor sits on the card's name with draggable=false, never around the draggable card.
